definition_en: a small house, especially in the countryside, or a small house used for holidays
core_image: 一栋石头小屋，茅草屋顶上飘着一缕细烟
scene: 雨落在茅草顶上，烟囱冒出细细一缕烟。 They spent the summer in a small cottage by the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 cottage 指「乡村小屋」（第 1 个义项：乡下的小房子）；句意是他们在海边的一间小屋度过了夏天。

senses.title: A small country house
senses.definition: a small simple house, especially in the countryside
senses.definitionCN: 尤指乡下的简朴小房子
senses.example: They spent the summer in a small cottage by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边的一间小屋度过了夏天。
senses.why: Small walls and a low roof keep a country life warm.
senses.whyCN: 矮墙低顶，把乡间的生活捂得暖暖的。

senses.title: A house for holidays
senses.definition: a small house that people rent or keep for short holidays
senses.definitionCN: 人们租用或留着短期度假的小房子
senses.example: We rented a cottage in the hills for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在山里租了一间小屋住了一周。
senses.why: A holiday needs a roof smaller than the life you left behind.
senses.whyCN: 度假需要一个比原先生活更小的屋顶。

intro.en: Cottage goes back to Old English cot, a small hut, with the French ending -age added in medieval times.
intro.cn: cottage 可追溯到古英语 cot（小屋），中世纪时加上法语词尾 -age。

items.en: Cot meant a small hut or shelter.
items.cn: cot 意为小茅屋或遮蔽处。

items.en: Cotagium named a small dwelling with a little land.
items.cn: cotagium 指带一小块土地的小住所。

items.en: Cottage named the house of a country worker.
items.cn: cottage 指乡间劳动者的住房。

items.en: English cottage meant a small rural house.
items.cn: 英语 cottage 指乡间的小房子。

items.en: It now also names small houses kept for holidays.
items.cn: 今天它也指留着度假用的小屋。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words near the shape of cottage, and the meaning group names other small dwellings.
note.cn: 形近组收集形状接近 cottage 的短词，近义组列出其他小型住所。

entries.definition: a place of higher or further education
entries.definitionCN: 高等教育或继续教育的场所

entries.definition: a poor farm worker with a small cottage
entries.definitionCN: 只有一间小屋的贫苦农业雇工

entries.definition: a small shelter for birds or animals
a small simple wooden house
a very small and simple shelter
a small house used for hunting or holidays

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a stone wall and a low roof, then move to a rented holiday house in the hills.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从石头墙和低屋顶开始，再到山里租来的度假小屋。

normal.en: Cot is an old word for a small hut, and -age makes it a place.
normal.cn: cot 是表示小茅屋的古词，加 -age 就成了一个地方。

normal.en: A cottage is smaller than a house and warmer than a tent.
normal.cn: 小屋比房子小，却比帐篷暖和。

normal.en: Think of a low door, a small window and smoke from the chimney.
normal.cn: 想想一扇矮门、一扇小窗和烟囱里的烟。

normal.en: A cottage garden grows flowers beside the vegetables.
normal.cn: 乡舍花园在蔬菜旁边种着花。

normal.en: Cottage and college look alike but live very different lives.
normal.cn: cottage 与 college 长得像，过的却是很不一样的日子。

abstract.en: Picture rain sliding down a roof of yellow straw.
abstract.cn: 想象雨水顺着金黄茅草屋顶滑下。

abstract.en: Picture one warm window in a dark green valley.
abstract.cn: 想象墨绿山谷里的一扇暖窗。

abstract.en: Picture a key too small to open anything but a cottage door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小得只能开小屋门的钥匙。

examples.en: They spent the summer in a small cottage by the sea.
examples.cn: 他们在海边的一间小屋度过了夏天。

examples.en: We rented a cottage in the hills for a week.
examples.cn: 我们在山里租了一间小屋住了一周。

examples.en: A narrow path leads to the old cottage.
examples.cn: 一条窄路通向那间老屋。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cottage 记成 cot（小床、小屋）加 tage：一张小床就能安顿下来的地方，就是村舍小屋。

root: 源自古英语 cot（小茅屋、棚舍），中世纪加法语词尾 -age，本指乡间劳动者的小住所，后泛指村舍与度假小屋。

sensesIntro.en: From a worker's small house in the country, to a small house rented for a few weeks.
sensesIntro.cn: 从乡间劳动者的小住所，到租来住几周的小屋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone cottage with a low thatched roof and thin smoke.
core.cn: 核心意象：石头小屋，低矮的茅草顶上升起一缕细烟。

branches.en: A country family lives close to the ground and the weather.
branches.cn: 乡间人家贴着土地与天气生活。

branches.en: A visitor borrows that small life for a short time.
branches.cn: 来客短暂地借用那种小日子。

branches.en: Both are small roofs, one lived in and one borrowed.
branches.cn: 两者都是小屋顶，一个常住，一个借用。

branches.en: The garden and the chimney are part of its picture.
branches.cn: 花园与烟囱都是它画面的一部分。

branches.en: Holiday cottages keep old shapes for new guests.
branches.cn: 度假小屋用旧形状迎接新客人。

intro.en: Cottage joins the old base cot, a hut, with the French noun ending -age, meaning a place.
intro.cn: cottage 由古词基 cot（小屋）加法语名词词尾 -age（场所）构成。

latinIntro.en: The dwelling base cot- also appears in cot, cote and cottage.
latinIntro.cn: 表示住所的词基 cot- 也出现在 cot、cote 与 cottage 中。

items.meaning: a person who lives in a cottage
items.example: The cottager waved from the gate.
items.exampleCN: 住小屋的人在门口挥手。

items.meaning: work done at home in small units
items.meaningCN: 在家中分散进行的小规模生产
items.example: Weaving began as a cottage industry.
items.exampleCN: 织布最初是家庭手工业。

items.meaning: soft white cheese made at home
items.example: He ate cottage cheese for lunch.
The cottage garden smell of roses.
items.exampleCN: 乡舍花园里有玫瑰的香气。

items.meaning: a dish of meat under mashed potato
items.meaningCN: 上面铺土豆泥的肉馅饼
items.exampleCN: 她烤了一个肉馅土豆饼。

items.meaning: a small simple bed or hut
items.example: A cot stood by the wall.

definition_zh: 瞬间；片刻；立即的；即食的
definition_en: an extremely short moment, or something that happens or is ready at once
core_image: 快门按下的一瞬，飞溅的水珠停在半空中
scene: 厨房里水壶刚响，桌上的杯子还在晃。 The kettle boiled and the room went silent for an instant.
sceneCN: 这里 instant 是「一瞬」（第 1 个义项：极短的一刻），句意是水壶烧开，屋子里静了一瞬。画面里能看到的物件：水壶、杯子、水汽。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「立即」
由本词加拉丁词尾构成，义为「瞬间发生的」
由本词加 -y 构成，义为「紧迫；立即」

senses.title: A very short moment
senses.definition: an extremely short period of time, too short to measure
senses.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间，短到无法计量
senses.example: For an instant she thought the room was empty.
senses.exampleCN: 有一刹那她以为屋里没人。
senses.why: Latin instans means standing upon, pressing at this very moment; an instant is the point that presses on you now.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instans 意为「立于其上、就在此刻逼近」，instant 就是压到你眼前的那个点。

senses.title: Happening at once
senses.definition: happening or produced immediately, without delay
senses.definitionCN: 立即发生或产生的，没有延迟
senses.example: The film was an instant success with young viewers.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影在年轻观众中一举成功。
senses.why: The pressing moment becomes a quality: what happens in that moment is instant.
senses.whyCN: 「紧迫的时刻」变成一种性质：发生在那刻的事就是 instant。

senses.title: Ready with almost no preparation
senses.definition: food or drink that is ready in seconds, needing only water
senses.definitionCN: 只需加水几秒即可食用的食品或饮料
senses.example: He keeps a jar of instant coffee in the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 他抽屉里常放一罐速溶咖啡。
senses.why: Modern packaging applied the adjective to goods made to be ready in an instant.
senses.whyCN: 现代包装把这个形容词用于「一瞬即可备好」的商品。

intro.en: Instant is the Latin present participle of instare "to stand upon, press near", so it means "pressing on now".
intro.cn: instant 是拉丁语 instare「立于其上、逼近」的现在分词，意为「此刻正逼近的」。

items.en: Stare "to stand" is the base of a large family of position verbs.
items.cn: stare「站立」是一大群方位动词的根基。

items.en: Instare meant to stand upon, to be imminent, or to urge.
items.cn: instare 意为「立于其上、即将发生、催促」。

items.en: The participle instans "present, pressing" came to mean the present time.
items.cn: 分词 instans「当下的、紧迫的」后来被用来指「现在」。

items.en: Old French instant brought both noun and adjective into English.
items.cn: 古法语 instant 把名词与形容词一起带入英语。

items.en: Nineteenth and twentieth-century trade made instant a label for ready-made goods.
items.cn: 十九、二十世纪的商业让 instant 成为现成商品的标签。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the standing root; the near-meaning group holds other words for a very short time.
note.cn: 形近组共享「站立」词根；近义组收其他表示「极短时间」的词。

entries.definition: Standing together without change.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「恒定的」，字面是「站在一起」。

entries.definition: What stands under a thing, hence its matter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「物质」，字面是「站在下面的东西」。

entries.definition: Something standing in the way, with ob- against.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「障碍」，前缀 ob- 表「对着、挡住」。

entries.definition: A short point in time, slightly longer than an instant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「片刻」，比 instant 稍长。

entries.definition: A measured unit of time, more exact.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「秒」，是精确的计量单位。

entries.definition: A sudden burst of light used figuratively for a very short time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「闪光」，比喻极短的时间。

normalIntro.en: These hooks contrast instant with instance and keep the "pressing now" image.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子对比 instant 与 instance，并保留「此刻逼近」的意象。

normal.en: Instant has a t: a point of time; instance has a c: an example.
normal.cn: instant 带 t 是时间点；instance 带 c 是例子。

normal.en: The same participle once meant the present time.
normal.cn: 这个分词曾用来指「现在」。

normal.en: In an instant is the commonest phrase in this sense.
normal.cn: in an instant 是这一义项最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Instant coffee is coffee minus the waiting.
normal.cn: 速溶咖啡就是省去等待的咖啡。

normal.en: Instant success is rare and usually luckier than it looks.
normal.cn: 一举成名很少见，通常比看上去更靠运气。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of water frozen in mid-air.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水停在半空中。

abstract.en: An instant is the smallest room a decision can fit in.
abstract.cn: 瞬间是一个决定能容身的最小空间。

abstract.en: Every history is made of instants stacked like coins.
abstract.cn: 一切历史都由像硬币般叠起的瞬间构成。

examples.en: The room went dark for an instant.
examples.cn: 屋里黑了一瞬。

examples.en: She recognized him in an instant.
examples.cn: 她一眼就认出了他。

examples.en: Instant noodles are popular with students.
examples.cn: 方便面在学生中很受欢迎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因此谈的」——因此一谈就见分晓，就是一瞬间

root: 拉丁语 stare「站立」→ instare「立于其上、逼近」→ 现在分词 instans「当下的、紧迫的」→ 古法语 instant → 英语 instant，兼作名词「瞬间」与形容词「立即的」。与 instance、constant、distance 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a point of time, immediacy as a quality, and goods ready in seconds.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：一个时间点、作为性质的「立即」，以及几秒即成的商品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a water drop hangs frozen in the air after the shutter clicks.
core.cn: 核心意象：快门按下后，水珠凝在半空中。

branches.en: THE SHUTTER: a time too short to measure.
branches.cn: 快门这条线：短到无法计量的时间。

branches.en: THE APPLAUSE: success that comes at once.
branches.cn: 掌声这条线：立刻到来的成功。

branches.en: THE JAR: goods ready without waiting.
branches.cn: 罐子这条线：无需等待即成的商品。

branches.en: THE LINK: the moment and the quality share the idea of no delay.
branches.cn: 连接线：时间点与性质共享「没有延迟」。

branches.en: THE LABEL: trade made the adjective a packaging word.
branches.cn: 标签线：商业把它变成了包装用语。

intro.en: Instant is in- plus the Latin participle stem sta-nt-, literally "standing upon".
intro.cn: instant 是 in- 加拉丁分词词干 sta-nt-，字面是「立在其上的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin instare and the participle instans are both classical and well attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 instare 与分词 instans 都是古典且有充分记载的形式。

items.example: It marks standing right upon the moment.
items.exampleCN: 它标出「正压在这一刻上」。

items.example: The root is visible in station and stable.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根见于 station 与 stable。

items.example: It keeps the word a participle in form.
items.exampleCN: 它让这个词在形式上保持分词。

items.example: A longer adjective in technical use.
items.exampleCN: 技术语域中较长的形容词。

items.example: Con- gives the idea of together.
The root appears without a prefix.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根的无前缀形式。

definition_en: so silly or unreasonable that it deserves laughter
core_image: 戴着过大的帽子去开会的人
scene: 他戴着一顶过大的帽子走进会场，看上去十分可笑。 He wore a huge hat to the meeting and looked ridiculous.
sceneCN: 这里 ridiculous 是「可笑的」（第 1 个义项：荒谬到引人发笑）；句意：他戴着一顶过大的帽子走进会场，看上去十分可笑。

senses.title: Too silly to believe
senses.definition: so silly that it seems impossible
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢得让人觉得不可能
senses.example: It is ridiculous to blame the rain for your lateness.
senses.exampleCN: 把迟到归咎于下雨实在荒谬。
senses.why: The word comes from laughter at what is absurd.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源于对荒谬之事的发笑。

senses.title: Funny to look at
senses.definition: strange enough to make people laugh
senses.definitionCN: 古怪得令人发笑
senses.example: He looked ridiculous in that tiny jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着那件小小的外套显得很可笑。
senses.why: Something badly matched looks laughable.
senses.whyCN: 搭配不当的东西看起来就好笑。

senses.title: Wildly unreasonable
senses.definition: unreasonably large or small
senses.definitionCN: 大小得极不合理
senses.example: They asked a ridiculous price for the old bike.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为那辆旧自行车要了个离谱的价钱。
senses.why: A number beyond sense also earns a laugh.
senses.whyCN: 不合常理的数字同样引人发笑。

intro.en: Ridiculous comes from Latin ridiculus, laughable, from ridere, to laugh.
intro.cn: ridiculous 源自拉丁语 ridiculus（可笑的），来自 ridere（笑）。

items.en: Ridere means to laugh.
items.cn: ridere 意为笑。

items.en: Ridiculus means fit to be laughed at.
items.cn: ridiculus 意为值得被嘲笑的。

items.en: French ridicule carries the sense of mockery.
items.cn: 法语 ridicule 带有嘲弄之意。

items.en: English ridiculous means absurd.
items.cn: 英语 ridiculous 意为荒谬。

items.en: It also scolds wild prices and plans.
items.cn: 如今它也用来批评离谱的价格与计划。

note.en: Ridiculous points to laughter; absurd points to the lack of sense.
note.cn: ridiculous 指向发笑，absurd 指向缺乏道理。

entries.definition: to make fun of someone
in a laughable way
the quality of being absurd
completely unreasonable
showing little thought
so bad or odd that one laughs

normalIntro.en: Ridiculous describes what deserves a laugh.
normalIntro.cn: ridiculous 形容值得发笑的事。

normal.en: Ridicule is the verb that mocks.
normal.cn: ridicule 是表示嘲笑的动词。

normal.en: A ridiculous idea makes no sense.
normal.cn: ridiculous idea 毫无道理。

normal.en: That hat looks ridiculous on you.
normal.cn: 那顶帽子戴在你头上很可笑。

normal.en: A ridiculous price is far too high.
normal.cn: ridiculous price 高得离谱。

normal.en: Laughter is hidden inside the word.
normal.cn: 笑声藏在这个词里面。

abstract.en: Picture a clown at a serious meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小丑出现在严肃的会议上。

abstract.en: Imagine shoes three sizes too big.
abstract.cn: 想象一双大了三号的鞋。

abstract.en: Think of a price tag with too many zeros.
abstract.cn: 想象一张写着太多零的价签。

examples.en: The plan sounded ridiculous at first.
examples.cn: 这个计划起初听起来很荒唐。

examples.en: It is ridiculous to walk in this storm.
examples.cn: 在这种暴风雨里走路太荒唐了。

examples.en: She felt ridiculous in the wrong uniform.
examples.cn: 穿着错误的制服让她觉得很可笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ridi（笑）＋ culous」——让人忍不住笑出来的，就是荒谬可笑。

root: 拉丁语 ridere（笑）→ ridiculus（可笑的）→ 法语 ridicule → ridiculous，核心义「荒谬到引人发笑」。

sensesIntro.en: Ridiculous means silly enough to laugh at, funny in appearance, or wildly unreasonable.
sensesIntro.cn: ridiculous 意为愚蠢可笑、模样古怪，或离谱得不合理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a laugh rising at something absurd.
core.cn: 核心意象：面对荒谬之事升起的笑声。

branches.en: An absurd idea invites laughter.
branches.cn: 荒谬的想法招来笑声。

branches.en: A mismatched outfit looks funny.
branches.cn: 不搭的装扮看起来好笑。

branches.en: A wild price is laughably unreasonable.
branches.cn: 离谱的价格荒唐得可笑。

branches.en: Both a foolish plan and a strange look make us laugh.
branches.cn: 愚蠢的计划与古怪的模样都让人发笑。

branches.en: A funny look and a wild price both break good sense.
branches.cn: 古怪模样与离谱价格都违背常理。

intro.en: Ridiculous grows from the Latin root rid, to laugh.
intro.cn: ridiculous 由拉丁词根 rid（笑）生长而来。

latinIntro.en: Ridere gives ridiculus, and French carries ridicule into English.
latinIntro.cn: ridere 给出 ridiculus，法语又把 ridicule 带进英语。

items.example: Rid carries the idea of laughter.
Ridicule brings the word to English.

latinEntries.example: Ridere is the source of ridiculous.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ridere 是 ridiculous 的来源。

definition_zh: 王室的；皇家的；盛大的；王室成员
definition_en: belonging to or connected with a king or queen, or a member of a royal family
core_image: 王冠下的家族：一切属于国王与王后的人与物
scene: 王宫前举行了盛大的阅兵仪式，士兵们列队走过。 The royal family waved to the crowd from the palace balcony.
sceneCN: 这里 royal 是「王室的」（第 1 个义项：属于国王或女王及其家族）；句意：王室成员在王宫阳台上向人群挥手。

pos.zh: 王室的；皇家的；盛大的；庄严的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ty 后缀构成，义为「王室成员；版税」
由形容词加 -ly 后缀构成，义为「盛大地；庄严地」
与 royal 仅字母顺序不同，义为「忠诚的」，词源不同，属形近词

senses.title: Belonging to a king or queen
senses.definition: connected with or belonging to the king or queen of a country
senses.definitionCN: 与国王、女王或其家族相关或为其所有
senses.example: The royal family lives in a grand palace.
senses.exampleCN: 王室家族住在一座宏伟的宫殿里。
senses.why: The crown marks everything that belongs to the ruler, so the word points straight at the throne.
senses.whyCN: 王冠是统治者的标志，凡属君主与王族的都冠以这个词，直指王座。

senses.title: Founded or named by a monarch
senses.titleCN: 由君主敕建的；冠以 royal 之名的
senses.definition: given the name royal by a king or queen, often for an organization they support
senses.definitionCN: 由国王或女王授予 royal 称号的组织或机构
senses.example: She is a member of the Royal Society of Science.
senses.exampleCN: 她是皇家科学学会的成员。
senses.why: Monarchs grant their title to institutions as a mark of patronage, extending the crown's reach.
senses.whyCN: 君主把 royal 称号赐给受其庇护的机构，王冠的权威由此延伸到这些组织。

senses.title: Grand and splendid
senses.definition: very grand, impressive, or magnificent in appearance
senses.definitionCN: 外观上极为宏大、气派、令人印象深刻
senses.example: They gave us a royal welcome at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在门口给了我们盛大的欢迎。
senses.why: Everything the crown touches is expected to be splendid, so royal stretches to any magnificence.
senses.whyCN: 王冠所及之物都须气派非凡，royal 由此引申为一切盛大恢宏的场面。

senses.title: A member of the royal family
senses.definition: a person who belongs to a royal family, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 作名词用，指王族中的一员
senses.example: Crowds gathered to see the young royal at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 人群聚集在车站迎接这位年轻的王室成员。
senses.why: An adjective for the family becomes a noun for any person inside that family.
senses.whyCN: 形容家族的词顺势转指家族中的任何一个人。

intro.en: Royal comes through Old French from Latin regalis, meaning of a king, from rex, king.
intro.cn: royal 经古法语来自拉丁语 regalis（君王的），词根为 rex（国王）。

items.en: Regalis means of or belonging to a king, built on rex, the Latin word for king.
items.cn: 拉丁语 regalis 意为「属于国王的」，建立在 rex（国王）一词之上。

items.en: Old French kept the word as roial, carrying the same royal meaning.
items.cn: 古法语将该词承袭为 roial，王家的意义未变。

items.en: Royal entered English in the thirteenth century, competing with native kingly.
items.cn: royal 于十三世纪进入英语，与本族词 kingly 并存并用。

items.en: English monarchs began granting the title royal to institutions and ships.
items.cn: 英国君主开始把 royal 称号授予机构与舰船，扩大了该词的使用范围。

items.en: Royal now covers the family, its institutions, and any splendid occasion.
items.cn: 今天 royal 覆盖王室家族、其所属机构，以及一切盛大庄严的场合。

note.en: Royal has a famous look-alike with swapped letters and near-meaning words about monarchy.
note.cn: royal 有一个字母换位的著名形近词，近义词集中在君主题材的义场。

entries.definition: faithful to a person, country, or idea
entries.definitionCN: 忠诚的，与 royal 仅字母顺序互换，读音几乎相同但词源无关，属经典形近词

entries.definition: fitting for a king; splendid and dignified
entries.definitionCN: 帝王气派的；庄严华丽的，与 royal 同出拉丁语 rex，更侧重气质而非身份

entries.definition: actually existing; not imagined
entries.definitionCN: 真实的；实在的，与 royal 拼写仅差一字母，词源无关，只是形近

entries.definition: suitable for or like a king
entries.definitionCN: 国王般的；威严的，本族语说法，强调气质而不强调隶属关系

entries.definition: grand and impressive in appearance or manner
entries.definitionCN: 雄伟的；威严的，突出气势恢宏，不必与王族相关

entries.definition: related to an emperor or empire
entries.definitionCN: 帝国的；皇帝的，规模与级别高于国王，常用于帝国语境

normalIntro.en: Five ways to remember royal through the crown and its Latin root.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕王冠与其拉丁词根的记忆路径。

normal.en: ROYAL contains ROY, from Latin rex meaning king: the king's word.
normal.cn: ROYAL 里的 ROY 来自拉丁语 rex（国王），这个词本来就是「国王的」。

normal.en: ROYAL vs LOYAL: swap two letters and the crown becomes a promise.
normal.cn: ROYAL 与 LOYAL 互换两个字母，王冠就变成了忠诚的誓言，正巧王室最需要忠诚。

normal.en: The Royal Navy sails with the crown painted on its ships.
normal.cn: 皇家海军的舰船上画着王冠，royal 一词随王冠出海。

normal.en: REGAL and ROYAL are cousins: both grow from Latin rex.
normal.cn: REGAL 与 ROYAL 是同根兄弟，都长自拉丁语 rex（国王）。

normal.en: A royal welcome rolls out the red carpet, as grand as any palace.
normal.cn: royal welcome 铺开红地毯，排场比得上王宫大典。

abstract.en: Picture a golden crown floating above everything it owns.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶金冠悬浮在它所拥有的一切之上。

abstract.en: Hear trumpets announce a splendid procession entering the gate.
abstract.cn: 听号角齐鸣，盛大仪仗浩浩荡荡走进大门。

abstract.en: See a family tree with a crown at the very top.
abstract.cn: 看一棵家谱树，树顶端端正正放着一顶王冠。

examples.en: The royal palace opens to visitors every summer.
examples.cn: 王宫每年夏天向游客开放。

examples.en: She received a royal welcome when she returned home.
examples.cn: 她回乡时受到了盛大的欢迎。

examples.en: Thousands waited to catch a glimpse of the royals.
examples.cn: 数千人等候一睹王室成员的风采。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「若爱哦」——王室若爱民，民众自然拥戴；royal 读音近似「若爱哦」

root: 源自拉丁语 rex（国王）的派生形容词 regalis（君王的），经古法语 roial 于十三世纪进入英语；与 regal 同根，与 loyal 仅拼写相近而词源无关。

sensesIntro.en: Royal moves from belonging to the crown, to institutions it names, to any splendid grandeur, and finally to the people themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: royal 从「属于王冠」出发，扩展到受封的组织、盛大排场，最后转指王室成员本人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: everything under the golden crown
core.cn: 核心意象：金冠之下的一切人与物

branches.en: The crown marks the king, the queen, and all who belong to them.
branches.cn: 王冠标记国王、女王以及所有属于他们的人。

branches.en: Monarchs lend the crown's name to institutions they protect.
branches.cn: 君主把王冠之名借给它所庇护的机构。

branches.en: What the crown touches must look magnificent.
branches.cn: 王冠所及之物必须气派非凡。

branches.en: The adjective for the family turns into a noun for its members.
branches.cn: 形容家族的形容词转指家族中的成员。

branches.en: A titled society and a grand feast both borrow the crown's splendor.
branches.cn: 受封的学会与盛大的宴席都在借用王冠的光彩。

intro.en: Royal builds a small family around the Latin root for king.
intro.cn: royal 围绕拉丁语「国王」词根构成一个小小的词族。

latinIntro.en: Royal comes from Latin regalis, built on rex, so it has close Latin-rooted relatives.
latinIntro.cn: royal 来自拉丁语 regalis（建立在 rex 之上），故有拉丁同根近亲。

items.meaning: members of a royal family; a payment for each copy of a book sold
items.meaningCN: 王室成员（总称）；版税（按销量付给作者的费用）
items.example: The writer earns a royalty on every copy sold.
items.exampleCN: 每卖出一本书，作者都能拿到版税。

items.meaning: in a grand or splendid way
items.example: We were royally entertained at the banquet.
items.exampleCN: 宴会上我们受到了盛大的款待。

items.meaningCN: 帝王气派的；庄严的（与 royal 同根的更文学说法）
items.example: She made a regal entrance in a long gown.
items.exampleCN: 她身穿长裙、仪态庄严地入场。

items.meaning: the crown, scepter, and other emblems of royalty
items.meaningCN: 王权的标志物（王冠、权杖等）
items.example: The coronation displayed the ancient regalia.
items.exampleCN: 加冕典礼上陈列了古老的王权标志物。

items.meaningCN: 国王（拉丁语名词，整个词族的源头）
items.example: Rex appears in the Latin title of a king.
items.exampleCN: rex 出现在国王的拉丁语头衔中。

items.meaning: a ruler acting for a sovereign in a colony
items.meaningCN: 总督；代替君主统治殖民地的官员
items.example: The viceroy governed the colony for the king.
items.exampleCN: 总督代国王治理殖民地。

items.meaning: a supporter of a king or queen
items.example: Royalists gathered to defend the palace.
items.exampleCN: 保皇派聚集起来保卫王宫。

items.meaning: the king or queen and their relatives
items.example: The royal family appears on the balcony each year.
items.exampleCN: 王室家族每年都在阳台上亮相。

items.meaning: an order made by a monarch
items.meaningCN: 敕令；由君主颁布的法令
items.example: A royal decree established the new order.
items.exampleCN: 一道敕令确立了新秩序。

items.meaning: the highest hand in the card game of poker
items.meaningCN: 同花大顺（扑克牌中最大的牌型）
items.example: He won the game with a royal flush.
items.exampleCN: 他靠同花大顺赢了这局牌。

latinEntries.meaning: of or belonging to a king
latinEntries.meaningCN: 君王的；属于国王的（royal 的直接来源）

definition_en: what is inside or written in something, or feeling happy and satisfied
core_image: 翻开一本书，满页的字与图铺在眼前
scene: 她翻到目录，看这本书到底讲了哪些章节。 The content of the report surprised everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 content 指「内容」（第 1 个义项：书或文件里写的东西）；句意是这份报告的内容让所有人吃惊。

senses.title: What is written or shown
senses.definition: the ideas, words or images held in a book, film or site
senses.definitionCN: 书、影片或网站里承载的想法、文字或图像
senses.example: The content of the letter was short but clear.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信的内容简短而清楚。
senses.why: A cover tells you nothing about what it protects.
senses.whyCN: 封面对于它所保护的东西一无所知。

senses.title: The amount inside
senses.definition: the amount of a substance held in something
senses.definitionCN: 某物内部所含某种物质的量
senses.example: Check the sugar content on the label.
senses.exampleCN: 看看标签上的含糖量。
senses.why: What a thing is made of can be printed as a number.
senses.whyCN: 一件东西由什么构成，能印成一个数字。

senses.title: Quietly satisfied
senses.definition: happy with what one has and not wanting more
senses.definitionCN: 对已有的事物满意而不求更多
senses.example: She felt content with her small garden.
senses.exampleCN: 她对自己那片小花园感到满足。
senses.why: The word that means held together also means at rest.
senses.whyCN: 表示「拢在一起」的那个词，也表示安心。

intro.en: Content comes from Latin contentus, the past participle of continere, held together, and so also satisfied.
intro.cn: content 来自拉丁语 contentus，是 continere（拢住）的过去分词，因而也含有「被满足」之意。

items.en: Continere meant to hold things together inside.
items.cn: continere 意为把东西拢在里面。

items.en: Contentus described something contained, and later a mind at rest.
items.cn: contentus 描述被容纳之物，后来也指安定的心。

items.en: The noun named what a thing held within it.
items.cn: 相应的名词指事物内部所盛的东西。

items.en: French content kept both the inside and the satisfied senses.
items.cn: 法语 content 同时保留内部与满足两层意思。

items.en: English content first meant what a writing held.
items.cn: 英语 content 最初指文字作品所包含的东西。

items.en: It now covers media material and the amount of a substance.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖媒体素材与某种物质的含量。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the contain- family, and the meaning group names other words for what fills a thing or a mind.
note.cn: 形近组共享 contain- 词族，近义组列出其他表示充盈之物或满足之情的词。

entries.definition: the things held inside something
to have something inside
feeling happy and satisfied
pleased because a need or wish is met
entries.definitionCN: 因需求得到满足而高兴的

entries.definition: the material that something is made of
facts or things used to make something

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a page full of print, then move to a number on a label and to a person who wants nothing more.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从印满字的书页开始，再到标签上的一个数字，最后到一个别无所求的人。

normal.en: Content is what a container holds, moved from things to words.
normal.cn: content 就是容器里的东西，从实物挪到了文字上。

normal.en: A thick cover hides a thin content, or a rich one.
normal.cn: 厚封面既可能盖着单薄的内容，也可能盖着丰富的内涵。

normal.en: Sugar content is content you can measure in grams.
normal.cn: 含糖量是能用克称出来的内容。

normal.en: To be content is to have enough and stop counting.
normal.cn: 满足就是觉得够了，不再往下数。

normal.en: The same word fills a book and calms a heart.
normal.cn: 同一个词既装满一本书，也安顿一颗心。

abstract.en: Picture an open book with dense small print.
abstract.cn: 想象一本摊开的书，满是细密的字。

abstract.en: Picture a label with one number circled.
abstract.cn: 想象一张标签上有一个被圈出的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a person sitting still with a cup of tea.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人端着一杯茶静静坐着。

examples.en: The content of the course is mostly practical.
examples.cn: 这门课的内容大多是实用的。

examples.en: This juice has a high sugar content.
examples.cn: 这种果汁含糖量很高。

examples.en: He was content to wait another hour.
examples.cn: 他愿意再等一个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 content 记成 con（一起）加 tent（握住）：被一起握住、兜在里面的东西就是内容，兜得刚好就叫满足。

root: 源自拉丁语 contentus（continere 拢住 的过去分词），本义是被盛住、被围住，后指容器里的内容、物质的含量，又引申为内心安定的满足。

sensesIntro.en: From the words held inside a cover, to the grams held in a bottle, and to a heart that holds enough.
sensesIntro.cn: 从封面里装着的文字，到瓶子里装着的克数，最后到一颗装得下「够了」的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open book whose pages are packed with print.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本摊开的书，书页上排满文字。

branches.en: The first sense is everything the cover keeps from view.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是封面挡在视线之外的一切。

branches.en: The second sense weighs the inside in grams.
branches.cn: 第二个义项用克来称里面的东西。

branches.en: The third sense says a person can also be full and at rest.
branches.cn: 第三个义项说人也能装满而安歇。

branches.en: Both senses ask what a thing is carrying inside it.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在问一件东西里面装着什么。

branches.en: Enough sugar and enough peace are both a kind of measure.
branches.cn: 足够的糖与足够的安宁，都是一种度量。

intro.en: Content is built on Latin com-, together, plus tenere, to hold: what is held inside.
intro.cn: content 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 tenere（握住）构成，指被拢在里面的东西。

latinIntro.en: The Latin hold base tent- also appears in contain, retention and maintain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的握持词基 tent- 也出现在 contain、retention 与 maintain 中。

items.meaningCN: 被拢在某物里面的东西
items.example: The content of the box was a mystery.
items.exampleCN: 盒子里装的是什么仍是个谜。

items.meaning: the list or the things inside
items.example: She checked the contents of the bag.
The cat looked contented by the fire.
items.exampleCN: 那只猫在炉火边显得很满足。

items.meaning: the state of wanting nothing more
items.example: A simple meal gave him contentment.
items.exampleCN: 一顿简单的饭就让他很知足。

items.meaning: an object that holds other things

definition_zh: 非法的；违法的；不合法的
definition_en: forbidden by law or by official rules, and punishable if done
core_image: 大楼门口一块被红笔划掉的车位牌，写着此处禁止停车
scene: 市中心的巷口立着一块新做的牌子。 Parking there is illegal after eight in the evening, so drivers keep moving past it.
sceneCN: 这里 illegal 指「非法的、违法的」（第 1 个义项：法律明令禁止），句意是晚上八点后在那里停车属违法，于是司机们一路开过去。画面里有巷口、新牌子和不肯停下的车。

pos.zh: 形容词：非法的、违法的、不合法的

collocations.phrase: it is illegal to do something

collocations.zh: 严格禁止的、绝对违法的

senses.title: Forbidden by law
senses.definition: against the law and punishable by the courts
senses.definitionCN: 违反法律、会被法院处罚的
senses.example: It is illegal to sell alcohol to children.
senses.exampleCN: 向儿童出售酒类是违法的。
senses.why: The prefix in- here works as a pure negative, so the word simply says that a thing does not fall inside the law.
senses.whyCN: 这里的前缀表否定，词义就是「这件事不在法律许可的范围之内」。

senses.title: Against the rules of a sport or game
senses.definition: not allowed by the rules of a game or competition
senses.definitionCN: 违反比赛规则的
senses.example: The referee ruled that the tackle was illegal.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判判定这次抢球属于犯规。
senses.why: Sport has its own rule book, and since the word points at any codified rule, it slid easily from courts of law to fields of play.
senses.whyCN: 体育有自己的规则册，而这个词指向一切成文规则，于是自然从法庭滑到了球场。

senses.title: Not officially approved
senses.definition: done without official permission, especially in building or trade
senses.definitionCN: 未获官方许可而做的，尤指建筑或经营
senses.example: An illegal extension was built onto the back of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 房子后面加建了一间未经批准的屋子。
senses.why: Modern life adds licences and permits to law, and anything done outside them borrows the same word.
senses.whyCN: 现代生活给法律添上执照与许可，凡在许可之外做的事也借用同一个词。

intro.en: Illegal joins a Latin negative prefix to the Latin word for law; it entered English through French in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: illegal 由拉丁语否定前缀与拉丁语「法律」一词合成，中世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: Lex, legis meant law, whether a statute or a binding custom of the community.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lex、属格 legis 意为「法律」，既指成文法，也指共同体约束性的习俗。

items.en: Legalis described what belonged to law and was lawful, a word already carrying a clear yes or no.
items.cn: legalis 形容「属于法律的、合法的」，本身已带有明确的是非判断。

items.en: Adding the negative in-, scribes formed illegals to name what fell outside the law.
items.cn: 加上否定前缀 in- 后，抄写者们造出 illegals，用来指法律之外的事。

items.en: French carried the form as illegal, and its legal clerks used it constantly in court records.
items.cn: 法语以 illegal 的形式承下此词，司法文书里频繁使用。

items.en: English took it up in the sixteenth century and broadened it to rules of sports, trades and building.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪收入该词，并把适用范围扩展到体育规则、行业与建筑。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the il- family born from the same negative prefix; the near-meaning group collects other strong words for what is not allowed.
note.cn: 形近组收同样由否定前缀 il- 生成的家族词；近义组收其他表示「不被允许」的强词。

entries.definition: Not following reason; it shares the same il- prefix and the same negative force.
entries.definitionCN: 不合逻辑的；共用同一个 il- 否定前缀与否定意味。

entries.definition: Impossible to read, built with the same prefix but applied to writing.
entries.definitionCN: 难以辨认的，前缀相同但用于书写。

entries.definition: Not allowed or not valid, a close cousin that adds the idea of legitimacy.
entries.definitionCN: 不正当的、无效的，多了一层「正当性」的意思。

entries.definition: Not permitted by law, the plainest native synonym of illegal.
entries.definitionCN: 不合法的，是 illegal 最直白的同义词。

entries.definition: Relating to crime; stronger, since it names punishable wrongdoing.
entries.definitionCN: 犯罪的；语气更重，因为它直接指向应受刑罚的恶行。

entries.definition: Not allowed by someone in authority, often a household or a school.
entries.definitionCN: 被禁止的，多用于当权者的规定，如家中或校内。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the Latin law root and the loud negative prefix to fix the spelling and the meaning together.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借拉丁语「法律」词根与显眼的否定前缀，把拼写与词义一起钉住。

normal.en: il- is a negative prefix, and legal is law, so illegal is literally not legal.
normal.cn: il- 是否定前缀，legal 是法律上的，所以 illegal 字面上就是「不合法」。

normal.en: The double l is the trick of spelling: the in- of negation folds into the l of legal.
normal.cn: 拼写难点在双 l：否定的 in- 在 l 前同化成 il-。

normal.en: The same il- hides in illogical and illegible, so any il- word is a no.
normal.cn: 同一个 il- 也藏在 illogical 与 illegible 里，凡以 il- 开头都是「不」。

normal.en: Say it with the stress on the second beat: il-LEE-gal, like LEAR in legal.
normal.cn: 重音落在第二拍：il-LEE-gal，与 legal 里的 LE- 呼应。

normal.en: Remember the traffic sign with the red circle and a slash: that circle is illegal in picture form.
normal.cn: 记住交通牌上带斜杠的红圈：那个圈就是 illegal 的图解。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn in chalk around the law; everything outside the line is not banned by nature, only by that line.
abstract.cn: 想象用粉笔绕法律画了一圈：圈外的事本身并非天理不容，只是被那条线挡住。

abstract.en: The word never denies that an act happens; it only reports that the law refuses to approve of it.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不否认事情真的发生了，只说法律不肯点头。

abstract.en: A prefix as small as two letters can turn a permission into a prohibition, which shows how thin the line between yes and no is.
abstract.cn: 两个字母的前缀就能把允许翻成禁止，由此可见允与禁之间的界线有多薄。

examples.en: It is illegal to drive without a licence.
examples.cn: 无证驾驶是违法的。

examples.en: The factory was fined for illegal waste dumping.
examples.cn: 这家工厂因非法倾倒废物被罚款。

examples.en: Officials promised to close the illegal market within a week.
examples.cn: 官员承诺一周内取缔这个非法市场。

dict_mnemonic.text: il 不 + legal 合法的——不合法的，字面就是「不合法」

root: 拉丁语 lex（属格 legis）「法律」→ legalis「合法的」，加否定前缀 in-（在 l 前同化为 il-）成 illegals，经古法语 illegal 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: what the law forbids, what the rules of a game forbid, and what lacks official approval.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：法律禁止的、比赛规则禁止的，以及缺少官方批准的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red line drawn around the law, with everything beyond it closed off.
core.cn: 核心意象：绕法律画出一道红线，线外之事全部封闭。

branches.en: THE LAW LINE: selling to children or driving unlicensed is against statute.
branches.cn: 法律线：向儿童售酒、无照驾驶都触犯法条。

branches.en: THE FIELD LINE: a rough tackle is illegal under the rules of football.
branches.cn: 球场线：足球里粗野抢球按规则属于犯规。

branches.en: THE PERMIT LINE: an extension built without papers is illegal even if nobody complains.
branches.cn: 许可线：没有手续的加建，即使无人投诉也属违建。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT LINE: both senses need an authority to say no.
branches.cn: 裁决线：两种用法都需要一个权威来判定「不行」。

branches.en: THE PAPER LINE: licences and statutes are the documents the word quietly points at.
branches.cn: 文书线：执照与法规正是这个词默默指向的纸面依据。

intro.en: Illegal is a clean prefix-plus-root pattern: a Latin negative, a Latin law root, and English endings built on both.
intro.cn: illegal 是干净的前缀加词根结构：拉丁语否定前缀、拉丁语法律词根，以及在这两者上长出的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The negative in- and the law root lex are both attested in Latin, and the assimilation of n to l is a regular sound change.
latinIntro.cn: 否定前缀 in- 与法律词根 lex 在拉丁语中都有文献，n 同化为 l 是规律性的语音变化。

items.example: The same prefix appears in illogical.
items.exampleCN: 同一个前缀也见于 illogical。

items.example: The contract is legal and binding.
items.exampleCN: 这份合同合法且具约束力。

items.example: Illegal parking blocks the fire lane.
items.exampleCN: 违章停车堵住了消防通道。

items.example: He parked illegally outside the school.
items.exampleCN: 他把车违法停在了学校门外。

items.meaning: the state of being against law
items.example: The court examined the illegality of the order.
items.exampleCN: 法院审查了这道命令的违法性。

items.example: She had a legitimate reason to complain.
Unlawful entry carries a heavy fine.

latinEntries.meaning: a proposer or maker of laws

definition_en: a person who supports a person, group, or idea
core_image: 看台上举起围巾、为球队呐喊的人群
scene: 许多支持者在外面等候。 Many supporters waited outside.
sceneCN: 这里 supporter 是「支持者」（第 1 个义项）；句意：许多支持者在外面等候。

senses.title: A person who backs something
senses.definition: someone who helps or agrees with a cause
senses.definitionCN: 帮助或赞同某项事业的人
senses.example: Many supporters waited outside.
senses.exampleCN: 许多支持者在外面等候。
senses.why: This is the general sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是通用义项。

senses.title: A fan of a team
senses.definition: a fan who follows a sports team
senses.definitionCN: 追随某支运动队的粉丝
senses.example: He is a loyal supporter of the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他是这支球队的忠实球迷。
senses.why: This is the sports sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是体育语境义项。

intro.en: Supporter is support plus -er, a person who supports.
intro.cn: supporter 是 support 加 -er，表示支持的人。

items.en: Supportare meant to carry from below.
items.cn: supportare 意为从下面承载。

items.en: Supporter meant to bear or help.
items.cn: supporter 意为承载或帮助。

items.en: Supporter meant a person who helps.
items.cn: supporter 指提供帮助的人。

items.en: It named backers of causes and teams.
items.cn: 它指事业与球队的支持者。

items.en: It remains common in sport.
items.cn: 它在体育中尤为常见。

note.en: Supporter is compared with look-alike words and with words for fans and backers.
note.cn: 把 supporter 与形近词以及表示拥护者的词作比较。

giving help
helping or secondary
a keen follower
a person who supports a plan
a person who speaks for a cause

normalIntro.en: A supporter is someone who stands behind you, not in front.
normalIntro.cn: 支持者站在你身后，而不是挡在你前面。

normal.en: Many supporters waited outside.
normal.cn: 许多支持者在外面等候。

normal.en: He is a loyal supporter of the team.

normal.en: Supporters cheered as the team scored.
normal.cn: 球队得分时球迷们欢呼。

normal.en: She is a strong supporter of the school.
normal.cn: 她是这所学校的坚定支持者。

abstract.en: A supporter lends belief when yours is thin.
abstract.cn: 支持者在你信心稀薄时借给你信念。

abstract.en: Every cause is carried by quiet supporters.
abstract.cn: 每项事业都由安静的支持者托起。

abstract.en: To support is to stand behind, not above.
abstract.cn: 支持，是站在身后，而不是站在头上。

examples.en: Many supporters waited outside.
examples.cn: 许多支持者在外面等候。

examples.en: He is a loyal supporter of the team.

definition_en: almost entirely, or in effect, or by means of a computer simulation
core_image: 一间空荡荡的教室，屏幕上却坐满了人
scene: 考试前一周，老师发现班里的座位几乎空了一半，学生都在线上听课。 Virtually every student had watched the lecture online before the test.
sceneCN: 这里 virtually 是「几乎、差不多」（第 1 个义项：接近全部但未绝对如此）；句意为考试前几乎每个学生都在网上看过这节课。空了一半的教室正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去后缀 -ly 构成的形容词，义为「实质上的；虚拟的」
同源名词，义为「美德；优点」
加后缀 -ize 构成，义为「虚拟化」

senses.title: Almost, for practical purposes
senses.definition: almost completely, with only a very small exception
senses.definitionCN: 几乎完全如此，只有极小的例外
senses.example: Virtually every student had watched the lecture online before the test.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前几乎每个学生都在网上看过这节课。
senses.why: From virtue in the old sense of power or effect: what holds in effect holds almost everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 源自古义为「效力」的 virtue：在效力上成立的，就几乎处处成立。

senses.title: In effect, though not in name
senses.definition: in practice or in effect, even if not formally so
senses.definitionCN: 实际上如此，尽管名义上并非如此
senses.example: The two plans are virtually the same.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个计划实际上是一样的。
senses.why: When a difference exists only on paper, the adverb says the effect is the same.
senses.whyCN: 当差别只存在于纸面上时，这个副词就说明效果相同。

senses.title: By computer simulation
senses.definition: by means of a computer model or online environment rather than in person
senses.definitionCN: 通过计算机模型或网络环境而非实体方式
senses.example: The whole factory was tested virtually before it was built.
senses.exampleCN: 整座工厂在建造前先做了虚拟测试。
senses.why: Modern computing gave virtual a new sense, and the adverb followed it into the lab.
senses.whyCN: 现代计算给了 virtual 新义，副词也随它走进了实验室。

senses.title: By remote or online means
senses.definition: through online channels instead of a physical place
senses.definitionCN: 通过线上渠道而非实体场所
senses.example: Half the team works virtually from other cities.
senses.exampleCN: 团队一半的人在其他城市远程工作。
senses.why: A meeting held on screens is held in effect, so the adverb covers remote work.
senses.whyCN: 在屏幕上开的会实际上也是会，副词因此也涵盖远程工作。

senses.title: Nearly, but not quite
senses.definition: close to a state without reaching it fully
senses.definitionCN: 接近某状态但尚未完全达到
senses.example: The old road is virtually gone under the new houses.
senses.exampleCN: 那条老路在新房子下几乎不见了。
senses.why: The word keeps a small door open, since virtually stops short of completely.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始终留着一道小门，因为 virtually 并不等于 completely。

intro.en: Virtually is virtual plus -ly; virtual comes from virtue, once meaning power or effect.
intro.cn: virtually 是 virtual 加 -ly；virtual 来自 virtue，古义为力量、效力。

items.en: Virtus meant worth, courage, and power, from vir, a man.
items.cn: virtus 意为价值、勇气与力量，源自 vir（男子）。

items.en: French vertu kept the sense of power or efficacy.
items.cn: 法语 vertu 保留了「力量、效力」之义。

items.en: English virtue covered moral worth and also active power.
items.cn: 中世纪英语的 virtue 兼指德行与实效力。

items.en: Virtual, and then virtually, meant effective in practice though not in name.
items.cn: virtual 及 virtually 表示名义上不是而实际上有效。

items.en: Computing added the sense of simulated by machine.
items.cn: 计算技术增加了「由机器模拟」之义。

note.en: The first group holds the virtual family, the second the adverbs of nearness and reality.
note.cn: 第一组是 virtual 词族，第二组是表示「近乎」与「实际」的副词。

entries.definition: effective in practice
moral goodness
to make simulated
a highly skilled performer
very nearly
in practice, nearly
close to but not fully

normalIntro.en: Power in the old sense became effect in practice, and then the world seen on screens.
normalIntro.cn: 古义的力量变成实际效力，再变成屏幕上所见的那个世界。

normal.en: Virtual plus -ly gives the adverb; nothing changes in the stem.
normal.cn: virtual 加 -ly 即副词，词干不变。

normal.en: Virtually every goes together in reports and studies.
normal.cn: 报告与研究里常用 virtually every。

normal.en: Virtually is not exactly: the door to completely stays ajar.
normal.cn: virtually 并不等于 exactly，通往 completely 的门没全关。

normal.en: The word starts with virtue, not with virus.
normal.cn: 这个词开头是 virtue，不是 virus。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable: VIR-tu-al-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节：VIR-tu-al-ly。

abstract.en: See half-empty seats and lit screens.
abstract.cn: 想一半空着的座位与亮着的屏幕。

abstract.en: Picture a factory tested in a model first.
abstract.cn: 想工厂先在模型里被检验一遍。

abstract.en: Hear a voice on a headset saying it is almost done.
abstract.cn: 听耳机里的声音说差不多完成了。

examples.en: The town was virtually cut off by the snow.
examples.cn: 大雪几乎把这座小镇与外界隔绝。

examples.en: Virtually all the tickets were sold by noon.
examples.cn: 几乎所有票在中午前就卖光了。

examples.en: They met virtually for the first three months.
examples.cn: 头三个月他们都是线上见面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「蜗牛其实」——蜗牛其实几乎不往前走，看着像没动。

root: 拉丁语 vir（男子）→ virtus（价值、力量）→ 古法语 vertu → virtue → virtual + -ly → virtually

sensesIntro.en: One adverb says almost, says in effect, and says through a screen: three ways of nearly being true.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个副词既说「几乎」，也说「实际上」，还说「隔着屏幕」，都是「近乎成真」的三种方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: empty seats, screens filled with faces.
core.cn: 核心意象：空座位与坐满屏幕的人脸。

branches.en: The almost branch: nearly every student, nearly the same, nearly gone.
branches.cn: 近乎分支：几乎每个学生、几乎一样、几乎消失。

branches.en: The effect branch: two plans alike in practice.
branches.cn: 效力分支：两个计划实际一样。

branches.en: The model branch: a factory tested on a computer.
branches.cn: 模型分支：在计算机里测试的工厂。

branches.en: The remote branch: a team spread across cities.
branches.cn: 远程分支：分散在各地办公的团队。

branches.en: The old road branch: a path lost under houses.
branches.cn: 老路分支：被房屋盖掉的路。

intro.en: The stem virt- means worth or power; -ual makes the adjective and -ly the adverb.
intro.cn: 词干 virt- 意为价值或力量，-ual 构成形容词，-ly 构成副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin virtus, from vir, man, meant worth and power; English virtual turned power into practical effect, and computing turned effect into simulation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 virtus（源自 vir「男子」）意为价值与力量；英语 virtual 把力量转为实际效力，计算技术又把效力转为模拟。

items.example: Virt- holds the sense of power.
Virtual means having the power in effect.
items.exampleCN: virtual 意为在效力上具备。

items.example: Virtually says it holds in effect.
items.exampleCN: virtually 表示在效果上成立。

items.example: Vir is the oldest link in the chain.
items.exampleCN: vir 是这条链上最早的环节。
practically 与 virtually 意义交叠。
virtually 不到 completely 的程度。

definition_en: to cut something with a heavy blow, to cut food into small pieces, or a small piece of meat cut with a rib
core_image: 一把菜刀落在砧板上，把肉剁成两半
scene: 厨房里飘着洋葱味，砧板响个不停。 She chopped the onions into small pieces.
sceneCN: 这里 chopped 是 chop 的过去式，指「切碎」（第 2 个义项：把食物切成小块）；句意是她把洋葱切成了小块。

senses.title: To cut with a heavy blow
senses.definition: to cut something with a heavy blow from an axe or a large knife
senses.definitionCN: 用斧头或大刀重重砍下
senses.example: He chopped the branch off the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那根树枝从树上砍了下来。
senses.why: Middle English choppen imitated the short heavy sound of a blade striking wood.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 choppen 模仿刀刃击木时短促沉重的声音。

senses.title: To cut food small
senses.definition: to cut food into small pieces with quick heavy blows
senses.definitionCN: 用快速有力的刀法把食物切成小块
senses.example: She chopped the onions into small pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 她把洋葱切成了小块。
senses.why: The same short blow moved from firewood to the kitchen board.
senses.whyCN: 同样短促的砍击从木柴移到了厨房砧板。

senses.title: A piece of meat on a rib
senses.definition: a small piece of meat cut together with a rib bone
senses.definitionCN: 带肋骨一起切下的一小块肉
senses.example: We had lamb chops for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 我们晚饭吃了羊排。
senses.why: A chop is literally a piece chopped off the carcass.
senses.whyCN: chop 字面上就是从整只牲畜身上剁下来的一块。

intro.en: Chop probably began as a sound word for a short heavy blow.
intro.cn: chop 最初很可能是一个模仿短促沉重砍击的拟声词。

items.en: The shape of the word echoes a blade striking wood.
items.cn: 这个词的声音模仿刀刃击木。

items.en: Choppen meant to cut with repeated heavy blows.
items.cn: choppen 意为用反复的重击来砍。

items.en: The verb spread from firewood to meat and vegetables.
items.cn: 这个动词从木柴扩展到肉类与蔬菜。

items.en: The noun named a rib piece cut off the carcass.
items.cn: 名词指从整只牲畜上剁下的带骨肉块。

items.en: Compounds gave chopsticks, chopper and the adjective choppy.
items.cn: 复合构词又生出 chopsticks、chopper 与形容词 choppy。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the short ch spelling, while the meaning group names ways of cutting.
note.cn: 形近组保持短促的 ch 拼写，近义组列出各种切割方式。

entries.definition: a small piece broken off something
a place where goods are sold
to crack or redden from cold
to divide something with a blade
to cut into thin flat pieces
to cut food into very small bits
entries.definitionCN: 把食物切成极小的碎末

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the sound of the blade, the kitchen board and the meat sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用刀声、厨房砧板以及排骨义。

normal.en: Say chop twice quickly and you hear an axe on a log.
normal.cn: 快速连说两次 chop，就听见斧头落在木头上的声音。

normal.en: Chop wood is the wood sense, chop onions is the kitchen sense, and both are short blows.
normal.cn: chop wood 是劈柴义，chop onions 是厨房义，两者都是短促的砍击。

normal.en: A pork chop is a piece chopped off, so the noun keeps the verb image.
normal.cn: a pork chop 就是剁下来的一块，名词保留了动词的意象。

normal.en: Chop down adds down, and the tree falls in the direction of the blow.
normal.cn: chop down 加上 down，树便朝砍击的方向倒下。

normal.en: Chopsticks and chopper both start from the same short stem.
normal.cn: chopsticks 与 chopper 都从同一个短词干出发。

abstract.en: Picture a blade biting into a log with a dull thud.
abstract.cn: 想象刀刃咬进木头，发出一声闷响。

abstract.en: Picture a board covered with neat piles of diced onion.
abstract.cn: 想象砧板上是一小堆一小堆切好的洋葱丁。

abstract.en: Picture a thick chop bone showing at the edge of the meat.
abstract.cn: 想象肉块边缘露出一截粗大的骨头。

examples.en: He chopped wood for the fire all morning.
examples.cn: 他整个上午都在劈柴生火。

examples.en: Add two chopped carrots to the pot.
examples.cn: 往锅里加两根切碎的胡萝卜。

examples.en: The pork chop was thick and juicy.
examples.cn: 那块猪排又厚又多汁。

dict_mnemonic.text: chop 读起来就像刀落砧板的一声：剁。

root: 源自中古英语 choppen（砍、剁），可能模仿刀斧砍击的声音，与 chap 相关。

sensesIntro.en: A short heavy blow gives the cutting sense, which moves to the kitchen and then to the piece of meat cut off.
sensesIntro.cn: 短促的重击先给出砍的动作，再移到厨房，最后指剁下来的那块肉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade falling once on a wooden board.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀刃在木板上落下一次。

branches.en: The axe sense is the oldest and the most physical.
branches.cn: 斧头义最古老，也最具体。

branches.en: The same blow works on onions and carrots.
branches.cn: 同样的砍击用在洋葱与胡萝卜上。

branches.en: The noun names the piece that the blow leaves.
branches.cn: 名词指这一刀之后留下的那块肉。

branches.en: Wood and food share one verb of short strokes.
branches.cn: 木柴与食物共用一个短促下刀的动词。

branches.en: The cut food and the cut meat sit side by side.
branches.cn: 切好的菜与剁下的肉彼此相邻。

intro.en: The short stem chop carries the verb, its inflections and three familiar compounds.
intro.cn: 短词干 chop 支撑动词、各种屈折形式以及三个常见复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and partly imitative, so no Latin root is involved.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语且带拟声成分，不涉及拉丁词根。

items.meaning: to cut with a heavy blow

items.example: The chopper hung by the stove.
The lake was choppy that day.
He ate the noodles with chopsticks.

items.meaning: a tool or person that acts

latinEntries.example: Choppen is the recorded source of chop.
latinEntries.exampleCN: choppen 是 chop 有记录的来源。

definition_zh: 断定；得出结论；结束；缔结
definition_en: to decide something after considering facts, or to bring something to an end
core_image: 一段长路走到尽头，回望时把整条路线看清
scene: 听完双方陈述，法官合上卷宗。 The judge concluded that the evidence was weak.
sceneCN: 这里 conclude 指「断定」（第 1 个义项：根据事实作出判断）；句意是法官断定证据不足。

pos.zh: 断定；得出结论；结束；缔结

senses.title: Reach a judgment
senses.definition: to decide that something is true after thinking about the facts
senses.definitionCN: 在思考事实之后判定某事为真
senses.example: We concluded that the plan was too risky.
senses.exampleCN: 我们断定这个计划风险太大。
senses.why: When the evidence is all in, the mind shuts the case and settles.
senses.whyCN: 证据齐了，心就合上案卷，作出定论。

senses.title: Bring to an end
senses.definition: to finish an event, speech or piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 结束一个活动、演讲或文章
senses.example: The meeting concluded at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 会议在中午结束。
senses.why: To close a matter is the same motion as closing a door.
senses.whyCN: 关闭一件事，和关上一扇门是同一个动作。

senses.title: Arrange a formal agreement
senses.definition: to complete a treaty, deal or agreement formally
senses.definitionCN: 正式完成条约、交易或协议
senses.example: The two countries concluded a trade agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 两国缔结了一项贸易协定。
senses.why: A deal is closed like a box, and once shut it is binding.
senses.whyCN: 交易像箱子一样被合上，一旦合上便有约束力。

intro.en: Conclude comes from Latin concludere, to shut up together, from com-, together, and claudere, to close.
intro.cn: conclude 来自拉丁语 concludere（一起关上），由 com-（一起）与 claudere（关闭）构成。

items.en: Claudere meant to close or to shut.
items.cn: claudere 意为关闭或合上。

items.en: Concludere meant to shut something in or to end it.
items.cn: concludere 意为把某物关起来或结束它。

items.en: Conclusio named a closing or a final inference.
items.cn: conclusio 指收尾或最终的推论。

items.en: Old French conclure meant to finish or to decide.
items.cn: 古法语 conclure 意为结束或决定。

items.en: English conclude took both the ending and the reasoning senses.
items.cn: 英语 conclude 同时接纳了结束与推理两种含义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to conclude, and the meaning group names other words for deciding or ending.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 conclude 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示断定与结束的词。

entries.definition: to have something as a part
to keep someone or something out
proving something beyond doubt
to choose after thinking
to bring something to an end
to reach an opinion from evidence

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a case file being closed, then move to a meeting ending and a treaty signed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从合上案卷开始，再走到会议结束与条约签署。

normal.en: Con- is together and clude is to close, so conclude is to close everything up.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，clude 是关闭，conclude 就是把一切合上。

normal.en: Include and exclude also carry the same closing base.
normal.cn: include 与 exclude 也带着同一个关闭词基。

normal.en: A judge concludes when the evidence has been shut into one story.
normal.cn: 当证据被合进一个说法，法官就作出断定。

normal.en: A speech concludes with a last line, as a box closes with a lid.
normal.cn: 演讲以最后一句话收尾，如同箱子合上盖子。

normal.en: To conclude a deal is to close it so no one can add a term.
normal.cn: 达成交易就是把它合上，谁也不能再加条款。

abstract.en: Picture a thick folder closing on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚卷宗在桌上合上。

abstract.en: Picture a road reaching its last stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路走到最后一块石头。

abstract.en: Picture two hands shaking as a door shuts behind them.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手相握，身后的门合上。

examples.en: The report concluded that the bridge was safe.
examples.cn: 报告断定这座桥是安全的。

examples.en: She concluded her talk with a short story.
examples.cn: 她用一个短故事结束了演讲。

examples.en: The two firms concluded a deal last week.
examples.cn: 两家公司上周达成了一笔交易。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conclude 记成 con（一起）加 clude（关闭）：把事情一起合上，就是结束，也是作出结论。

root: 源自拉丁语 concludere（com 一起 + claudere 关闭），本义是合上、关起来，后引申为结束、缔结与得出结论。

sensesIntro.en: From shutting a case, to closing an event, and finally to sealing an agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 从合上案卷，到结束一场活动，最后到封定一份协议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long road reaching its end, and the whole route seen at one glance.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长路走到尽头，回望时一眼看清整条路线。

branches.en: The judgment sense comes from closing the evidence into one view.
branches.cn: 断定义来自把证据合进一个看法。

branches.en: The ending sense is the most literal closing.
branches.cn: 结束义是最字面的合上。

branches.en: A formal deal is closed so that it stands.
branches.cn: 正式交易被合上，才能成立。

branches.en: A speech and an argument both end when the speaker closes them.
branches.cn: 演讲与论证都在说话人合上时结束。

branches.en: Ending and sealing both mean no more changes.
branches.cn: 结束与封定都意味着不再更改。

intro.en: Conclude is built on Latin com-, together, plus claudere, to close.
intro.cn: conclude 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 claudere（关闭）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin close base clud- also gives include, exclude and seclude.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的关闭词基 clud- 还给出 include、exclude 与 seclude。

items.example: The chapter concludes with a question.
items.exampleCN: 这一章以一个问句结束。

items.example: The conclusion follows from the data.

items.exampleCN: 测试确凿地证明了这一点。

items.example: They questioned the conclusiveness of the study.
items.exampleCN: 他们质疑这项研究的决定性。

items.meaning: not leading to a clear result

definition_zh: 女性的；雌性的；女性；雌性动物
definition_en: of the sex that can bear young, a woman or girl, or a female animal
core_image: 花园里那只雌孔雀没有开屏，却安静地立在栅栏边
scene: 花园里那只雌孔雀没有开屏，却安静地立在栅栏边。 The female peacock stood quietly by the fence.
sceneCN: 这里 female 是「雌性的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：那只雌孔雀安静地站在栅栏边。

senses.title: Of women
senses.definition: of or relating to women or girls
senses.definitionCN: 与女性或女孩有关的
senses.example: The female engineer led the team.
senses.exampleCN: 那位女工程师带领团队。
senses.why: This is the human use of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这是该形容词用于人类的义项。

senses.title: Of female animals
senses.definition: of the sex in animals that produces eggs
senses.definitionCN: 动物中产卵的性别
senses.example: A female bird builds the nest here.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，雌鸟负责筑巢。
senses.why: Biology uses the word across species.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用该词指各个物种。

senses.title: A woman or female animal
senses.definition: a person or animal of the female sex
senses.definitionCN: 女性的人或雌性动物
senses.example: The audience was mostly female.
senses.exampleCN: 观众大多是女性。
senses.why: The adjective also stands alone as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 该形容词也可单独作名词使用。

intro.en: Female comes from Latin femella, a young woman, a small form of femina, woman.
intro.cn: female 源自拉丁语 femella（年轻女子），是 femina（女人）的指小形式。

items.en: Femina meant a woman.
items.cn: femina 意为女人。

items.en: Femella meant a young woman.
items.cn: femella 意为年轻女子。

items.en: Femelle named a female animal.
items.cn: femelle 指雌性动物。

items.en: Female entered English with a spelling changed by folk memory of male.
items.cn: female 进入英语，拼写受到 male 一词的民间联想影响。

items.en: The word now describes people, animals, and connectors.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词可形容人、动物与接口。

note.en: Female is compared with similar-looking words and with words for women.
note.cn: 把 female 与形近词以及表示女性的词作比较。

entries.definition: of the sex that does not bear young
having qualities associated with women
the state of being female
an adult female human
a polite word for a woman
a female child

normalIntro.en: Female describes women and egg-producing animals, and can stand as a noun.
normalIntro.cn: female 形容女性与产卵的动物，也可单独作名词。

normal.en: Female and male are a natural pair.
normal.cn: female 与 male 是一对自然的对应词。

normal.en: The word is not spelled with a hyphen.
normal.cn: 这个词的拼写中没有连字符。

normal.en: Female can describe people, animals, and even plugs.
normal.cn: female 可形容人、动物，甚至插接口。

normal.en: Feminine describes qualities, while female describes sex.
normal.cn: feminine 描述气质，female 描述性别。

normal.en: Femaleness names the state of being female.
normal.cn: femaleness 指女性的状态。

abstract.en: The spelling changed to match male, though the roots differ.
abstract.cn: 拼写为配合 male 而改变，尽管两者词源不同。

abstract.en: A word for sex also became a word for social roles.
abstract.cn: 表示性别的词也变成了表示社会角色的词。

abstract.en: Naming sex is simple; naming its meaning is not.
abstract.cn: 指出性别很简单，解释其意义却不容易。

examples.en: The female engineer led the team.
examples.cn: 那位女工程师带领团队。

examples.en: A female bird builds the nest here.
examples.cn: 在这里，雌鸟负责筑巢。

examples.en: The audience was mostly female.
examples.cn: 观众大多是女性。

dict_mnemonic.text: female 源自拉丁语 femella（年轻女子），拼写后来受 male 影响，但两者并无共同词源。

root: 源自拉丁语 femina（女人）的指小形式 femella，核心义「女性或雌性」。

sensesIntro.en: Female means of women, of egg-producing animals, or a woman or female animal.
sensesIntro.cn: female 意为女性的、雌性的，或女性与雌性动物。

core.en: The sex that bears young, applied to people and animals.
core.cn: 能孕育后代的性别，适用于人与动物。

branches.en: The adjective for women and girls.
branches.cn: 形容女性与女孩的形容词。

branches.en: The adjective for egg-producing animals.
branches.cn: 形容产卵动物的形容词。

branches.en: A noun for a woman or female animal.
branches.cn: 表示女性或雌性动物的名词。

branches.en: The adjective and noun both name female people.
branches.cn: 形容词与名词都可指女性。

branches.en: In biology the noun is used across species.
branches.cn: 在生物学中该名词跨物种使用。

intro.en: Female belongs to the femina family, which also gives feminine and feminist.
intro.cn: female 属于 femina 词族，同族还有 feminine 与 feminist。

latinIntro.en: Latin femina and femella are the historical sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 femina 与 femella 是历史来源。

items.example: The study measured neither femaleness nor maleness.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究既不测量女性特质也不测量男性特质。

items.example: The room has a feminine style.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间有女性化的风格。

items.example: She refused to define femininity for others.
items.exampleCN: 她拒绝替别人定义女性气质。
女权主义改变了许多法律。
她是一位知名的女权主义者。

items.example: The design feminizes the old uniform.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计让旧制服更具女性风格。

items.example: The feminization of the profession happened slowly.
items.exampleCN: 这一职业的女性化过程发生得很缓慢。

definition_zh: 稀有的；罕见的；半熟的；稀薄的
definition_en: not common or not happening often; cooked lightly so the inside stays red; thin and not dense, of air
core_image: 空荡展厅里唯一一件孤零零的展品
scene: 空旷的展厅里只摆着一件展品，四周安静得能听见脚步。 Such a rare bird is seen only once in a lifetime.
sceneCN: 这里 rare 是「稀有的」（第 1 个义项：不常见、很少发生）；句意为这样稀有的鸟一生只能见到一次。画面里可留意：空荡的展厅、唯一的展品、安静的脚步。

pos.zh: 稀有的；罕见的；半熟的；稀薄的

derivatives.zh: rare 加 -fy 与 -ed，指变得稀薄的

senses.title: Uncommon
senses.definition: not found, seen or happening often; existing in small numbers
senses.definitionCN: 不常被发现、看见或发生；数量很少
senses.example: Such a rare bird is seen only once in a lifetime.
senses.exampleCN: 这样稀有的鸟一生只能见到一次。
senses.why: Latin rarus meant thinly spread, and the English word kept that picture of something scattered rather than plentiful.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rarus 意为分布稀疏，英语这个词保留了「零落而非充裕」的画面。

senses.title: Lightly cooked
senses.definition: cooked for a short time so that the inside is still red
senses.definitionCN: 烹制时间很短，内部仍然透红
senses.example: He likes his steak rare.
senses.exampleCN: 他喜欢半熟的牛排。
senses.why: English cooks used rare for meat left briefly on the heat, and the sense has stayed fixed in the kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 英语中的厨师用 rare 指在火上停留很短的肉，这层意思一直固定在厨房里。

senses.title: Thin, of air
senses.definition: thin and not dense, used especially of air at high places
senses.definitionCN: 稀薄而不浓密，尤用于高处的空气
senses.example: The air grows rare as you climb higher.
senses.exampleCN: 越往上爬，空气越稀薄。
senses.why: Air that is thinly spread is close to the original sense of rarus, so the word could describe atmosphere as well as objects.
senses.whyCN: 分布稀疏的空气贴近 rarus 的本义，因此这个词既能形容物件，也能形容大气。

intro.en: Rare comes from Latin rarus, thinly spread or uncommon, and English added the senses of thin air and lightly cooked meat.
intro.cn: rare 来自拉丁语 rarus（分布稀疏或不常见），英语又添上稀薄空气与半熟肉这两层意思。

items.en: Rarus meant thinly spread or uncommon, and it described both sparse things and rare events.
items.cn: rarus 意为分布稀疏或不常见，既形容稀疏之物，也形容罕见之事。

items.en: Old French borrowed it as rare and kept the sense of something seldom found.
items.cn: 古法语把它借作 rare，保留「难得一见」的意思。

items.en: Middle English rare applied the word to uncommon things and to thin air.
items.cn: 中古英语 rare 把这个词用于罕见之物与稀薄的空气。

items.en: The sense of lightly cooked meat grew in English kitchens, where rare described meat left briefly on the heat.
items.cn: 半熟肉的意思在英语的厨房里长成，rare 指在火上停留很短的肉。

items.en: Modern English uses rare for uncommon things, thin air, and meat cooked only briefly.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rare 指罕见之物、稀薄的空气，以及只略加烹制的肉。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base form and its close relatives; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is hard to find.
note.cn: 形近组收本词原形与近亲；近义组收表示「难觅」的词。

entries.definition: Not often.
Something uncommon, or the state of being uncommon.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见之物，或罕见的状态。

entries.definition: Thin, especially of air.
More uncommon.
Hard to find because there is little of it.
Not usual or not often seen.
Not ordinary, often in a noticeable way.
entries.definitionCN: 不普通的，常带引人注目之意。

entries.definition: Not happening often.

normalIntro.en: The word begins with scarcity, then takes in thin air and meat left briefly on the fire.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「稀少」开始，随后纳入稀薄的空气与在火上略过的肉。

normal.en: Rare and rarus both begin with the idea of something thinly spread.
normal.cn: rare 与 rarus 都从「某物分布稀疏」这一想法开始。

normal.en: A rare bird is one you seldom see, not one that cannot exist.
normal.cn: rare bird 是你很少见到的鸟，而不是不可能存在的鸟。

normal.en: Rare steak is cooked briefly, so the centre stays red.
normal.cn: rare steak 煎得很快，所以中心仍是红的。

normal.en: Rare air is thin air, as on a high mountain.
normal.cn: rare air 是稀薄的空气，就像高山上那样。

normal.en: Rarity is the noun and rarely the adverb, and both keep the sense of not often.
normal.cn: rarity 是名词，rarely 是副词，两者都保留「不常」的意思。

abstract.en: Rare things matter because they are few, not because they are better.
abstract.cn: 稀有之物重要，是因为它们少，而不是因为它们更好。

abstract.en: What is rare is defined by the many common things around it.
abstract.cn: 稀有之物是由周围众多常见之物界定出来的。

abstract.en: To call a moment rare is to say it will not come again soon.
abstract.cn: 称一个时刻 rare，是说它不会很快再来。

examples.en: This is a rare species found only on one island.
examples.cn: 这是只在一座岛上才能找到的稀有物种。

examples.en: He likes his steak rare.
examples.cn: 他喜欢半熟的牛排。

examples.en: The air grows rare as you climb higher.
examples.cn: 越往上爬，空气越稀薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「孤品」——展厅里只此一件，rare 就是稀有的、罕见的。

root: 拉丁语 rarus（稀疏、罕见）→ 古法语 rare → 现代英语 rare；同族有 rarely、rarity、rarefied。

sensesIntro.en: The core is scarcity; the senses divide into uncommon things, meat cooked briefly, and thin air.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「稀少」；义项分为罕见之物、略加烹制的肉，以及稀薄的空气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lonely object in a great empty hall.
core.cn: 核心意象：空荡大厅里孤零零的一件物品。

branches.en: a single gem in an empty hall
branches.cn: 空展厅里孤零零的一颗宝石

branches.en: a steak red at the centre
branches.cn: 中心仍透红的牛排

branches.en: mountain air that is hard to breathe
branches.cn: 让人呼吸吃力的山地稀薄空气

branches.en: scarcity of things and scarcity of air
branches.cn: 物的稀少与空气的稀薄

branches.en: uncommon in supply and uncommon in cooking
branches.cn: 数量上的罕见与烹制上的半熟

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built with English suffixes on the same root.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由同一词根上的英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin rarus, thinly spread, is the recorded source of the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rarus（分布稀疏）是这个词有记录可考的词源。

definition_zh: 强烈的；剧烈的；紧张的；热情的
definition_en: very great or extreme in strength, feeling, or degree
core_image: 灯丝被拧到最亮，光晕几乎要把镜头烧白
scene: 舞台上只剩一束聚光灯，演员额头冒汗，观众连呼吸都放轻了。 The heat in the small kitchen was so intense that the windows steamed up.
sceneCN: 这里 intense 是「强烈的、极度的」（第 1 个义项：强度极大），句意小厨房里热得厉害，窗户都起了雾。画面里的物件：聚光灯、额头的汗、起雾的窗。

pos.zh: 形容词：强烈的；剧烈的；紧张的；热情的

derivatives.zh: 由本词换后缀构成，义为「强度；强烈」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「强烈地」
由本词加 -ify 构成，义为「加强；加剧」
由同一词干构成，义为「紧张；内涵」

senses.title: Very strong in degree
senses.definition: extremely great in strength, force, or amount
senses.definitionCN: 在力度、力量或数量上极其之大
senses.example: The midday sun was so intense that the paint cracked.
senses.exampleCN: 中午的太阳太烈，油漆都裂开了。
senses.why: Latin intensus is the participle of intendere, "stretched tight".
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 intensus 是 intendere「绷紧」的分词。

senses.title: Deeply felt
senses.definition: felt very strongly, as of feelings, interest, or dislike
senses.definitionCN: 指情感、兴趣或厌恶等感受非常强烈
senses.example: She has an intense love of mountain air.
senses.exampleCN: 她极爱山里的空气。
senses.why: The same tightness is applied to feeling: emotions can be stretched to their limit.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「绷紧」被用到情感上：情绪也会绷到极限。

senses.title: Serious and concentrated
senses.definition: very serious, busy, and demanding of attention
senses.definitionCN: 非常严肃、繁忙，要求全神贯注
senses.example: The weeks before the exam were intense for everyone in the class.
senses.exampleCN: 考前那几周全班人都很紧张。
senses.why: Work and study borrow the word for a stretched state with no slack left.
senses.whyCN: 工作与学习借这个词形容毫无余裕的绷紧状态。

senses.title: Extreme in a worrying way
senses.definition: so extreme as to be frightening or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 极端到令人害怕或不快的程度
senses.example: The attack drew intense criticism from the town council.
senses.exampleCN: 那次攻击引来市议会猛烈的批评。
senses.why: Tightness can be unpleasant: stretched too far, strength becomes a threat.
senses.whyCN: 绷得太紧便会不好受：力量过头就成了威胁。

intro.en: Intense is a Latin participle of intendere "to stretch towards", so its core is tightness.
intro.cn: intense 是拉丁语 intendere「朝……伸展」的分词，因此其核心是「绷紧」。

items.en: Tendere "to stretch" with in- "towards" yields intendere, to strain forward.
items.cn: tendere「伸展」与 in-「朝向」构成 intendere「向前绷紧」。

items.en: Intensus described a bow or string pulled tight.
items.cn: intensus 形容被拉得很紧的弓或弦。

items.en: Late Latin extended the participle to light, heat, and emotions that reach a peak.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把这个分词扩展到达到顶点的光、热与情感。

items.en: French intense narrowed the meaning to things very great in degree.
items.cn: 法语 intense 把意义窄化为「程度极大之事」。

items.en: English uses intense for heat, pressure, feeling, and, loosely, for earnest people.
items.cn: 英语用 intense 形容热、压力、感受，口语中也形容过于认真的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the stretched root; the near-meaning group holds other words for great strength.
note.cn: 形近组共享「绷紧」词根；近义组收表示「强度大」的词。

entries.definition: Concentrated on one task, such as a course.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「集中的、强化的」，如强化课程。

entries.definition: The measurable strength of heat, light or feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「强度」，可测量的量。

entries.definition: Purpose, or else fixed and absorbed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「意图」，形容词义为「专注的」。

entries.definition: Violent and angry, often of animals or weather.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「凶猛的」，多指动物或天气。

entries.definition: Sharp and strong, often of pain or problems.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「剧烈的」，多形容疼痛或问题。

entries.definition: Great in feeling or seriousness rather than force.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，偏指情感或程度之深，而非力量之大。

normalIntro.en: The hooks hang on the image of a string pulled to its limit.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子挂在「绳子拉到极限」这一画面上。

normal.en: Intense is a string with no slack left.
normal.cn: intense 就是一根再没有余量的弦。

normal.en: Intense heat, intense pressure, intense competition: the word adds a peak.
normal.cn: 酷热、巨大压力、激烈竞争：这个词都添上一个「顶点」。

normal.en: Intensity is what intense measures.
normal.cn: intensity 是 intense 所衡量的那个量。

normal.en: Intensive study is short and hard; intense study feels full of pressure.
normal.cn: intensive 学习短而猛，intense 学习则是压得满满。

normal.en: An intense person is rarely bored.
normal.cn: 性格强烈的人很少觉得无聊。

abstract.en: Intensity is a fire you cannot look away from.
abstract.cn: 强度是一团你无法转开视线的火。

abstract.en: Anything stretched too long returns changed.
abstract.cn: 任何拉得过久的东西回来时都变了样。

abstract.en: The word asks not how much, but how tight.
abstract.cn: 这个词不问多少，只问绷得多紧。

examples.en: The pressure before the launch was intense.
examples.cn: 发射前的压力非常大。

examples.en: He felt an intense dislike of crowded rooms.
examples.cn: 他对拥挤的房间有强烈的厌恶。

examples.en: Competition for the scholarship is intense this year.
examples.cn: 今年奖学金的竞争十分激烈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因太死」——绷得太死太紧，所以强度极高

root: 拉丁语 tendere「伸展」→ in- + tendere → intendere「朝前绷紧」→ 分词 intensus「拉紧的」→ 古法语 intense → 英语 intense。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: extreme degree, deep feeling, tense work, and unpleasant violence.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：程度极高、情感浓烈、工作紧张，以及令人不适的猛烈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a filament turned to full brightness.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯丝被开到最亮。

branches.en: THE SUN AT NOON: heat and light reach their peak.
branches.cn: 正午太阳这条线：热与光达到顶点。

branches.en: THE LOVED AIR: feeling is stretched to its edge.
branches.cn: 山间空气这条线：情感被拉到边缘。

branches.en: THE EXAM WEEK: attention has no slack left.
branches.cn: 考试周这条线：注意力毫无余裕。

branches.en: THE HARSH ATTACK: strength turns into threat.
branches.cn: 猛烈攻击这条线：力量变为威胁。

branches.en: THE LINK: both describe being pushed near a limit.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都形容被推到接近极限。

intro.en: Intense = in- "towards" + tens- "stretch" + -e, with the Latin participle ending dropped.
intro.cn: intense = in-「朝向」+ tens-「伸展」+ -e，拉丁分词词尾已脱落。

latinIntro.en: Latin intendere and intensus are recorded; English remodelled the ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intendere 与 intensus 有记载，英语改铸了词尾。

items.example: It gives direction to the stretch.

items.exampleCN: 也见于 tension 与 tensor。

definition_en: material made from the skin of animals, articles made from it, or the material used before a noun
core_image: 一块鞣好的牛皮摊在木台上，边缘还留着刀痕
scene: 作坊里，匠人把一张厚皮按在木台上，用刀顺着边裁下。 The smell of new leather filled the small workshop.
sceneCN: 这里是「皮革」（第 1 个义项：动物皮制成的材料）；句意为新皮革的气味充满这间小作坊。可辨识画面：木台、厚皮、裁皮刀。

derivatives.zh: 由 leather 加 -y 构成，义为「像皮革的；坚韧的」
由 leather 加 -ette（仿制品）构成，义为「人造革」
由 leather 加 -en（由……制成的）构成，义为「皮革制的」（古旧用法）
由 leather 与 back 复合，义为「棱皮龟」

senses.title: Material made from animal skin
senses.definition: material made by treating the skin of animals so that it is soft and strong
senses.definitionCN: 把动物皮处理得柔软结实之后得到的材料
senses.example: The bag is made of soft brown leather.
senses.exampleCN: 这个包用柔软的棕色皮革制成。
senses.why: Old English leþer named the treated hide itself, and that material sense has stayed the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 leþer 指处理过的兽皮本身，这层材料义一直是这个词的中心。

senses.title: Articles made of leather
senses.definition: things made from leather, especially when spoken of in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 用皮革制成的物品，尤指用复数形式时
senses.example: He cleaned his leathers after the ride.
senses.exampleCN: 骑完车后他清理了皮衣。
senses.why: Because a material can stand for the things cut from it, tanned skins become leathers in the plural.
senses.whyCN: 材料可以代替用它制成的东西，鞣好的皮在复数里就成了皮衣、皮具。

senses.title: Used before a noun to mean made of leather
senses.definition: placed before another noun to say that the thing is made of leather
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示该物由皮革制成
senses.example: She wore a leather jacket in the cold wind.
senses.exampleCN: 寒风里她穿着皮夹克。
senses.why: English often lets a material noun work as a modifier, so leather needs no suffix to describe a jacket.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让材料名词直接作修饰语，所以 leather 不加后缀就能修饰 jacket。

intro.en: An Old English noun for treated hide is the direct source, and its Germanic shape is still easy to hear.
intro.cn: 一个指处理过兽皮的古英语名词是直接来源，它的日耳曼语形态至今仍容易辨认。

items.en: Leþer named the skin of an animal after treatment, and it is the direct source of the word.
items.cn: leþer 指处理之后的兽皮，是这个词的直接来源。

items.en: The Germanic form behind it is reconstructed as leþra-, with related words in other Germanic languages.
items.cn: 其背后的日耳曼语形式被重构为 leþra-，在其他日耳曼语言里有相关词。

items.en: The old word may be related to the idea of a hide, though the exact link is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个旧词可能与「兽皮」的观念有关，但具体联系并不确定。

items.en: Middle English kept leather for the material and began using it for goods made of it.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 leather 指材料，并开始用它指由它制成的物品。

items.en: Modern English uses leather for the material, for leather goods, and as a word placed before nouns.
items.cn: 现代英语用 leather 指材料、指皮具，也把它放在名词前作修饰。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built from leather and words with a similar shape; the near-meaning group collects other words for skins and leather types.
note.cn: 形近组收由 leather 构成的形式以及形状相近的词；近义组收表示兽皮与皮革种类的其他用词。

entries.definition: Tough and dry like leather.
A manufactured material made to look like leather.
entries.definitionCN: 做成皮革样子的人造材料。

entries.definition: The state of the air outside, sun, rain or wind.
entries.definitionCN: 户外空气的状态，晴、雨或风；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: One of the light growths covering a bird.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖鸟类身体的轻软生成物之一。

entries.definition: The skin of a large animal, raw or tanned.
entries.definitionCN: 大型动物的皮，生的或鞣过的。

entries.definition: The outer covering of a body, or material from it.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的外层覆盖物，或由此得来的材料。

entries.definition: Leather with a soft brushed surface.
entries.definitionCN: 表面经过打磨起绒的软革。

entries.definition: The soft hair covering an animal, or a coat made of it.
entries.definitionCN: 动物身上的软毛，或由此制成的衣物。

normalIntro.en: A noun of treated hide and four English endings that build qualities, imitations and compounds hold this word together.
normalIntro.cn: 一个指处理过兽皮的名词，与四个造出性质、仿制品及复合词的英语词尾，共同支撑着这个词。

normal.en: Old English leþer is the direct source, and the th sound in the middle has never changed.
normal.cn: 古英语 leþer 是直接来源，中间那个 th 音一直没变。

normal.en: Leathery adds -y: having the toughness and dryness of leather.
normal.cn: leathery 加 -y，意为具有皮革的坚韧与干燥。

normal.en: Leatherette adds -ette, a suffix for imitations, so it is leather that is not leather.
normal.cn: leatherette 加 -ette，这是表示仿制品的后缀，所以是「不是皮革的皮革」。

normal.en: Leatherback is leather plus back, naming a turtle with a tough shell instead of hard plates.
normal.cn: leatherback 是 leather 加 back，指背甲坚韧而非硬板的龟。

normal.en: In a leather jacket, leather works as a modifier without any suffix.
normal.cn: 在 a leather jacket 里，leather 不加后缀就作修饰语。

abstract.en: A material word can name the goods made from it, so leathers means leather clothes.
abstract.cn: 材料词可以指用它做成的东西，所以 leathers 指皮衣。

abstract.en: Toughness is the memory of a hide that had to protect an animal, carried into a jacket.
abstract.cn: 坚韧是兽皮曾保护过动物的记忆，被带进了一件夹克。

abstract.en: English rarely marks material with a suffix, so leather sits before a noun and quietly becomes an adjective.
abstract.cn: 英语很少用后缀标记材料，于是 leather 直接站在名词前，悄悄变成形容词。

examples.en: The bag is made of soft brown leather.
examples.cn: 这个包用柔软的棕色皮革制成。

examples.en: She wore a leather jacket in the cold wind.
examples.cn: 寒风里她穿着皮夹克。

examples.en: He cleaned his leathers after the ride.
examples.cn: 骑完车后他清理了皮衣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累着」——皮衣厚重，穿着走一天累着了；记住 leather 是皮革。

root: 古英语 leþer（处理过的兽皮），与日耳曼语中重构的 leþra- 同源；与拉丁语 corium 无关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is treated animal skin; the senses then add the plural goods made from it and its use as a word before nouns.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是处理过的兽皮；义项由此加上用复数表示的皮具，以及放在名词前作修饰的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tanned hide spread on a wooden bench, a knife at its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：木台上摊开的鞣制兽皮，边缘搁着裁皮刀。

branches.en: a hide being worked with a knife on a bench
branches.cn: 木台上被刀修整的兽皮

branches.en: a row of leather jackets hanging in a shop
branches.cn: 店里挂着的一排皮衣

branches.en: a jacket described by the material it is cut from
branches.cn: 用其材料来描述的夹克

branches.en: a wallet softened by years in a pocket
branches.cn: 在口袋里磨软的钱包

branches.en: a belt with a worn buckle, still strong
branches.cn: 扣子磨旧却仍结实的皮带

intro.en: An Old English noun of treated hide and four English endings that build qualities, imitations and compounds.
intro.cn: 一个指处理过兽皮的古英语名词，以及四个造出性质、仿制品与复合词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; Latin corium, a different word for hide, is not its source.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语；拉丁语 corium 是另一个表示兽皮的词，并非它的来源。

items.meaning: leather plus back, a kind of turtle
items.meaningCN: leather 与 back 复合，指一种龟

items.meaning: the upper shell of a turtle

definition_en: a thick strong wire or rope used to carry electricity or signals
core_image: 粗壮的金属线缆盘绕成圈
scene: 工人在路边挖开沟槽。 They laid a new cable under the street.
sceneCN: 这里 cable 是「电缆」（第 1 个义项：输送电力的粗线）；句意是他们在街道下面铺了新电缆。

derivatives.zh: 海底电报，经电缆传送的电文
索道，用缆绳牵引的运输装置

senses.title: A thick wire for power or signals
senses.definition: a bundle of wires covered in a thick protective cover
senses.definitionCN: 外面包着厚保护层的线束
senses.example: They laid a new cable under the street.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在街道下面铺了新电缆。
senses.why: The core image is a thick line that carries force from one place to another.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一根粗线，把力量从一处送到另一处。

senses.title: A strong thick rope
senses.definition: a very thick rope used to hold or pull heavy things
senses.definitionCN: 用来拉住或拖动重物的粗绳
senses.example: The ship was tied with a steel cable.
senses.exampleCN: 船用钢缆系住了。
senses.why: Before electricity, the word named the heavy rope on ships and bridges.
senses.whyCN: 在电出现之前，这个词指船和桥上的粗绳。

senses.title: A message sent by telegraph
senses.definition: a short message sent by telegraph under the sea
senses.definitionCN: 经海底电缆用电报发出的简短消息
senses.example: He sent a cable to his family.
senses.exampleCN: 他给家人发了一封电报。
senses.why: Messages travelled along submarine cables, so the cable lent its name to the message.
senses.whyCN: 消息沿着海底电缆传送，电缆的名字就借给了电文。

intro.en: Cable goes back through French to a Latin word for a halter.
intro.cn: cable 经法语上溯到拉丁语里表示缰绳的词。

items.en: capulum meant a halter or rope.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capulum 指缰绳或绳索。

items.en: cable named a strong rope.
items.cn: 古北法语 cable 指结实的粗绳。

items.en: cable was used for ships' ropes.
items.cn: 中古英语 cable 用于船上的缆绳。

items.en: Telegraph cables crossed the sea and cable meant a telegram.
items.cn: 十九世纪海底电报电缆横跨大洋，cable 也指电报。

items.en: Cable covers power lines, ropes, television and telegrams.
items.cn: 现代英语中 cable 兼指电力线、缆绳、有线电视与电报。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cable base; the near-meaning group gives other lines and ropes.
note.cn: 形近组共用 cable 词基；近义组是其他线绳类词。

a message sent by submarine cable
a ropeway for carrying loads
a thin metal thread carrying electricity
a thick cord of twisted fibres
a thin flexible rope or wire

normalIntro.en: Cable names a thick line that carries power, pulls loads or sends news.
normalIntro.cn: cable 指输送电力、牵引重物或传递消息的粗线。

normal.cn: 复数是 cables。

normal.en: Cable TV arrives through a cable.
normal.cn: cable TV 通过电缆传送。

normal.en: A cable car hangs from a cable.
normal.cn: 缆车悬挂在缆绳上。

normal.en: Send a cable means send a telegram.
normal.cn: send a cable 义为发电报。

normal.en: Cabling is the whole wiring system.

abstract.en: See a ship held steady by two taut ropes.

abstract.en: See a short message arriving from under the ocean.

sensesIntro.en: A power line, a heavy rope, and a message sent by telegraph.
sensesIntro.cn: 电力线、粗缆绳，以及经电报发出的消息。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick line coiled and ready to carry force.
core.cn: 核心意象：盘好的粗线，随时输送力量。

branches.en: a power cable
