intro.cn: cable 能与 car、way、gram 组成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin capulum, a halter or rope.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 capulum，意为缰绳或绳索。

definition_zh: 全体船员；机组人员；一组工作人员
definition_en: the people who work together on a ship, an aircraft or a job
core_image: 一条船上所有人各守其位，一起划桨、一起收帆
scene: 天刚亮，船上的人已经在各自的位置上忙起来。 The whole crew was on deck before sunrise.
sceneCN: 这里 crew 指「全体船员」（第 1 个义项：同一条船上一起工作的人）；句意是天还没亮，全体船员就已到了甲板上。

pos.zh: 全体船员；机组人员；一组工作人员

senses.title: The people on a ship
senses.definition: all the people who work on a ship
senses.definitionCN: 在一条船上工作的所有人
senses.example: The crew lowered the boat into the water.
senses.exampleCN: 船员们把小艇放下水。
senses.why: A ship cannot sail without many hands at many stations.
senses.whyCN: 没有许多人在许多位置上，船就开不动。

senses.title: The team on a plane
senses.definition: the people who fly and serve on an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 在飞机上驾驶与服务的人
senses.example: The crew welcomed us aboard.
senses.exampleCN: 机组人员欢迎我们登机。
senses.why: A plane repeats the old pattern of a ship in the air.
senses.whyCN: 飞机只是把船的老样子搬到了空中。

senses.title: A team on a job
senses.definition: a group of people working together on a particular job
senses.definitionCN: 为某项工作一起干活的一群人
senses.example: A camera crew filmed the whole scene.
senses.exampleCN: 一个摄制组拍下了整个场面。
senses.why: Any job that needs many hands forms a small company.
senses.whyCN: 任何需要许多双手的活儿，都会凑成一个小团体。

intro.en: Crew comes from Old French creue, a reinforcement, from Latin crescere, to grow.
intro.cn: crew 源自古法语 creue（增援），再往上是拉丁语 crescere（生长）。

items.en: Crescere meant to grow or increase.
items.cn: crescere 意为生长或增加。

items.en: Creue meant a reinforcement of soldiers.
items.cn: creue 指补充上来的兵员。

items.en: Crew named a band of soldiers or helpers.
items.cn: crew 指一队士兵或帮手。

items.en: It named the company that worked a ship.
items.cn: 它指在船上干活的那一队人。

items.en: It spread to aircraft and film teams.
items.cn: 它延伸到飞机与摄制组。

items.en: It now means any team working as one.
items.cn: 今天它指任何协同干活的一队人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -rew sound, and the meaning group names other groups of workers.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -rew 这一串读音，近义组列出其他干活的人群。

entries.definition: a metal pin turned to hold things
entries.definitionCN: 拧进去固定东西的金属钉

entries.definition: one member of a crew
having people on board to operate it
a group playing or working together
entries.definitionCN: 一起比赛或干活的一群人

entries.definition: all the workers of a place
a small group working or moving together
entries.definitionCN: 一起干活或行动的一小群人

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a rope on deck to a camera on a street.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从甲板上的一根绳，挪到街上的一台摄影机。

normal.en: Crew rhymes with few, and a few hands run a ship.
normal.cn: crew 与 few 押韵，几条汉子就能开一条船。

normal.en: One captain, one wheel, many hands.
normal.cn: 一个船长，一只舵轮，许多双手。

normal.en: The cabin crew are sailors who learned to fly.
normal.cn: 客舱乘务组就是学会飞的船员。

normal.en: A film crew is a ship that sails on streets.
normal.cn: 摄制组是一条在街上航行的船。

normal.en: Crew is the plural of no one person.
normal.cn: crew 从来不是一个人，它天生是一群。

abstract.en: Picture a row of hands pulling the same rope.
abstract.cn: 想象一排手拉着同一根绳。

abstract.en: Picture a cockpit lit before dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明前亮着灯的驾驶舱。

abstract.en: Picture a camera team moving like one body.
abstract.cn: 想象一个摄制组像一具身体那样移动。

examples.en: The crew worked through the night.
examples.cn: 全体船员干了一整夜。

examples.en: She joined the cabin crew last year.
examples.cn: 她去年当上了客舱乘务员。

examples.en: A film crew set up its cameras in the square.
examples.cn: 一个摄制组在广场上架起了摄影机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crew 记成一条船上的一排人：各站各位，同拉一根绳，这一整队人就是 crew。

root: 源自古法语 creue（增援、补充），再往上是拉丁语 crescere（生长、增加）；本义是补充上来的兵员，后指一同干活的一队人，尤其船上与机上的人。

sensesIntro.en: From the hands on a ship, to the team in the air, to any crew on a job.
sensesIntro.cn: 从船上的许多双手，到空中的机组，再到任何一项活儿里的工作队。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many hands on one rope at dawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明时许多只手拉着同一根绳。

branches.en: A ship needs many people at fixed posts.
branches.cn: 一条船需要许多人在固定位置上。

branches.en: An aircraft carries the same team into the sky.
branches.cn: 飞机把同样的一队人带上天空。

branches.en: Any shared job gathers its own small crew.
branches.cn: 任何共同的活儿都会聚起自己的小队。

branches.en: Ship and plane both run on a chain of orders.
branches.cn: 船和飞机都靠一条命令链运转。

branches.en: The word never names one person alone.
branches.cn: 这个词从不单独指一个人。

intro.en: Crew is a short word that builds many compounds, from crewman to aircrew.
intro.cn: crew 是个短词，却能组成许多复合词，从 crewman 到 aircrew。

latinIntro.en: Behind the French form lies Latin crescere, to grow, the same root as increase.
latinIntro.cn: 法语形式背后是拉丁语 crescere（生长），与 increase 同根。

items.exampleCN: 一名船员招手让我们上船。

items.example: He met his old crewmate at the dock.
items.exampleCN: 他在码头遇见了老同船伙伴。

items.example: A crewless boat crossed the bay.
items.exampleCN: 一条无人船驶过了海湾。

a round neck on a sweater

items.example: The sailor kept a crew cut.

definition_en: an official order, control over a group of people, or to order someone to do something
core_image: 军官抬手一声令下，整队人同时转身
scene: 队长举起手，所有人立刻停下脚步。 The officer gave a command and the soldiers stood still.
sceneCN: 这里 command 指「命令」（第 1 个义项：上级下达的指令）；句意是军官下达命令，士兵们站定不动。

senses.title: An official order
senses.definition: an order given by someone with authority
senses.definitionCN: 有权者下达的指令
senses.example: The general gave the command to advance.
senses.exampleCN: 将军下达了前进的命令。
senses.why: The earliest sense in English is a direct order from a leader.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在英语里最早的义项就是首领直接下达的指令。

senses.title: Control over a group
senses.definition: the power to direct people or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 指挥人员或掌控局面的权力
senses.example: She was in command of the whole fleet.
senses.exampleCN: 她指挥着整支舰队。
senses.why: Whoever gives the orders holds the power, so order becomes control.
senses.whyCN: 下达命令的人掌握着权力，于是命令变成了掌控。

senses.title: To order or deserve
senses.definition: to order someone to do something, or to deserve and receive respect
senses.definitionCN: 命令某人做事，或赢得并得到尊敬
senses.example: Her calm voice commanded respect.
senses.exampleCN: 她沉静的声音赢得了尊敬。
senses.why: Authority both issues orders and draws respect without asking.
senses.whyCN: 权威既下达命令，也不必请求就赢得尊敬。

intro.en: Command comes from Latin mandare, to entrust, strengthened by the prefix com-.
intro.cn: command 来自拉丁语 mandare（托付），并由前缀 com- 加强语气。

items.en: Mandare meant to hand something over or entrust a task.
items.cn: mandare 意为把东西交出去或把任务托付给人。

items.en: Commandare added com- and took on the sense of ordering.
items.cn: commandare 加上 com-，带上了下令的意味。

items.en: Old French comander meant to order and to entrust.
items.cn: 古法语 comander 兼有下令与托付之意。

items.en: English command entered as both a noun and a verb of authority.
items.cn: 英语 command 以名词与动词两种身份进入，都表示权威。

items.en: It widened to mastery of a language and to earning respect.
items.cn: 它的用法扩展到语言的掌握与赢得尊敬。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close in spelling to command, while the meaning group lists verbs of ordering and directing.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 command 拼写相近的词，近义组列出下令与指挥的动词。

entries.definition: to praise someone formally
to ask for something firmly
a remark about something
to tell someone to do something
to give someone clear directions
to control or manage an activity

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a voice giving an order, then move to the power behind it and to the respect it earns.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一声下令开始，再走到命令背后的权力与它赢得的敬意。

normal.en: Com- plus mandare, to entrust, means a task handed down with authority.
normal.cn: com- 加 mandare（托付），指带着权威交办下去的任务。

normal.en: The one in command is the one whose words end discussion.
normal.cn: 处于指挥位置的人，话一出口讨论就结束。

normal.en: A good command of English means the language obeys you.
normal.cn: 良好的英语运用能力，意味着这门语言听你调遣。

normal.en: Command respect is respect you never had to ask for.
normal.cn: 赢得尊敬，是你从不必开口索要的尊敬。

normal.en: Commander adds -er and becomes the person who commands.
normal.cn: commander 加 -er，就成了下命令的那个人。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand and a whole line turning at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起，整排人同时转身。

abstract.en: Picture a map table lit by one lamp on a ship's bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象舰桥上被一盏灯照亮的地图桌。

abstract.en: Picture a room falling silent when one person begins to speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人开口时，整个房间安静下来。

examples.en: The captain gave a short command and the crew moved.
examples.cn: 船长下达了简短命令，船员们行动起来。

examples.en: She has a good command of three languages.
examples.cn: 她精通三门语言。

examples.en: His honesty commanded the trust of everyone there.
examples.cn: 他的诚实赢得了在场每个人的信任。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 command 记成 com（一起）加 mand（手）：手一挥，所有人一起动，就是命令。

root: 源自拉丁语 mandare（托付），加前缀 com- 后成 commandare，本义是把任务交办下去，后引申为命令、指挥与掌握。

sensesIntro.en: From an order spoken aloud, to the power that backs it, and finally to the respect and mastery it brings.
sensesIntro.cn: 从说出口的命令，到支撑它的权力，再到它带来的敬意与掌握。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an officer raising a hand and a whole line turning as one.
core.cn: 核心意象：军官抬手一声令下，整队人同时转身。

branches.en: The spoken order is the sense that entered English first.
branches.cn: 说出口的命令是最早进入英语的义项。

branches.en: Control is what makes an order more than a request.
branches.cn: 正因为有掌控力，命令才不只是请求。

branches.en: The verb covers both ordering people and earning respect.
branches.cn: 动词义既包括对人下令，也包括赢得尊敬。

branches.en: An order and the power behind it are two views of one act.
branches.cn: 命令与它背后的权力，是同一动作的两个视角。

branches.en: Mastery of a language is control without a single shout.
branches.cn: 对一门语言的掌握，是一声不喊的掌控。

intro.en: Command is a free base that forms agent nouns with -er and abstract nouns with -ment.
intro.cn: command 是自由词基，用 -er 构成施动者名词，用 -ment 构成抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin mandare, to entrust, is the root shared with mandate and demand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mandare（托付）是与 mandate、demand 共有的词根。

items.meaning: several orders, or he gives an order
items.exampleCN: 这个系统接受语音指令。

items.example: He commanded the unit for two years.
Several commanders met at the base.
items.exampleCN: 几位指挥官在基地会面。

items.meaning: the officer in charge of a place

items.example: He spoke commandingly to the crowd.

definition_zh: 最小值；最低限度；最低点；极小值；最小的；最低的
definition_en: the smallest amount, level or point that is possible, allowed or reached, or the lowest value of a set or function
core_image: 量筒底部划着一道红线，任何水位都不能低于它
scene: 清晨的水库边，管理员看着水位尺上那道浅浅的红线，提醒同伴抽水不能低于这里。 The reservoir is kept at a minimum during the dry months.
sceneCN: 这里 minimum 是「最低水位、最低限度」（第 1 个义项：可能或允许的最小量）；句意为干旱月份水库水位被维持在最低限度。画面里可抓住的物件：水位尺、红线、抽水泵。

pos.zh: 最小值；最低限度；最低点；极小值

collocations.zh: 把某事物控制在最低限度

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 minim- 加后缀 -al 构成，义为「最小的；极少的」
由 minim- 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使减到最少」
由 minimize 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「最小化」
由 minimal 加 -ist 构成，指极简主义者或极简的

senses.title: The smallest possible amount
senses.definition: the smallest amount of something that is possible, needed or allowed
senses.definitionCN: 某事物可能、需要或被允许的最小数量
senses.example: Keep the noise to a minimum after ten.
senses.exampleCN: 十点以后把噪音降到最低。
senses.why: Latin minimum is the neuter form of minimus, the smallest, and it entered English as a noun for the least quantity that can be reached or permitted.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minimum 是 minimus（最小的）的中性形式，进入英语时就是一个名词，指能够达到或被允许的最小数量。

senses.title: The lowest point reached
senses.definition: the lowest level or point that a changing quantity falls to before it rises again
senses.definitionCN: 某个变化中的量在下落之后、回升之前所到的最低水平或位置
senses.example: The river reaches its minimum in late summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河在夏末降到最低水位。
senses.why: Anything that rises and falls traces a curve, and the bottom of that curve is naturally called its minimum; the word moves from an allowed limit to an observed low.
senses.whyCN: 凡是有起伏的东西都会画出曲线，曲线的最低处自然被叫作 minimum；词义于是从「被允许的下限」转到「观察到的低点」。

senses.title: Lowest allowed by a rule
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean the smallest or lowest that a rule, price or standard permits
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指规则、价格或标准所允许的最小或最低值
senses.example: The minimum age for driving is eighteen in many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 许多国家的驾车最低年龄是十八岁。
senses.why: English turns the noun into a modifier by placing it before another noun; minimum wage is the wage at the bottom of the permitted scale, with no ending added.
senses.whyCN: 英语把名词放到另一个名词前面就使它成为修饰语；minimum wage 就是允许范围最底端的工资，词形不加任何词尾。

senses.title: The lowest value of a set or function
senses.definition: the smallest value that a set of numbers or a mathematical function takes
senses.definitionCN: 一组数值或一个数学函数所能取到的最小值
senses.example: The curve has a minimum at the centre and rises on both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这条曲线在中央有极小值，两侧向上升高。
senses.why: Mathematics needed a precise name for the bottom of a graph, and it borrowed the Latin word unchanged; the everyday sense of a lower bound became a technical term.
senses.whyCN: 数学需要给图像的最低处一个精确的名字，于是原封不动地借用了这个拉丁词；日常的「下界」义由此变成了术语。

intro.en: Minimum came straight from Latin, where it was the neuter form of the word for smallest; English borrowed it in the seventeenth century as a noun for the least amount.
intro.cn: minimum 直接来自拉丁语，是「最小的」一词的中性形式；英语在十七世纪把它借来，作名词指最小量。

items.en: Parvus meant small; its comparative minor and superlative minimus are generally treated as suppletive forms, borrowed from a related root rather than built with a regular ending.
items.cn: parvus 意为「小的」；一般认为它的比较级 minor 与最高级 minimus 属于补充式形式，借自相关词根，而不是用规则词尾构成。

items.en: Minimus meant the smallest or least, and it supplied the top of the scale in phrases such as minimus natu, the youngest.
items.cn: minimus 意为最小的、最少的；在 minimus natu（最年幼者）这类说法里，它标出等级序列的最末端。

items.en: The neuter singular minimum was used as a noun for the smallest amount, and this exact form was taken over by English.
items.cn: 中性单数形式 minimum 被当作名词使用，指最小量；英语原样借用的正是这个形式。

items.en: Writers borrowed minimum in the seventeenth century, first in scientific and mathematical writing where a precise lower bound was needed.
items.cn: 十七世纪的作者借入 minimum，最早用在科学与数学写作中，因为那里需要一个精确的下界。

items.en: Modern English uses it as a noun and as a modifier, and keeps the Latin plural minima beside the English minimums.
items.cn: 现代英语让它作名词也作修饰语，并在英语复数 minimums 之外保留拉丁式复数 minima。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the Latin comparison of small; the near-meaning group collects other words for the least amount or the bottom of a scale.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁「小」的比较之上的形式；近义组收其他表示最小量或标度底端的词。

entries.definition: As small as possible; barely enough to count.
entries.definitionCN: 尽可能小的；刚刚够得上数的。

entries.definition: To reduce something to the smallest possible amount or level.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物减到尽可能小的数量或程度。

entries.definition: Smaller, less important, or not yet legally adult; it belongs to the same Latin comparison of small.
entries.definitionCN: 较小的、较次要的，或尚未成年的；它属于同一个拉丁「小」的比较系列。

entries.definition: A tiny amount, or a short note value in early music.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的量，或早期音乐中短小的音符时值。

entries.definition: The smallest amount or degree of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物最小的数量或程度。

entries.definition: The lowest level that prices or amounts are allowed to reach.
entries.definitionCN: 价格或数量被允许降到的最低水平。

entries.definition: The lowest point of something, especially of a changing situation.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物的最低点，尤指变化中的境况。

entries.definition: The lowest part or level of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的最下部或最低水平。

normalIntro.en: Minimum is the superlative of a Latin word for small, and its family keeps circling the idea of the least amount or the bottom of a scale.
normalIntro.cn: minimum 是拉丁语「小」一词的最高级形式，它的一族词始终围着「最小量」或「标度底端」打转。

normal.en: Minimus is Latin for smallest, and minimum is its neuter form, so the word already carries the comparison inside it.
normal.cn: minimus 是拉丁语「最小的」，minimum 是它的中性形式，所以这个词本身就带着比较。

normal.en: The min- root recurs in minor, minus and minute: all of them measure something smaller or less.
normal.cn: min- 这个词根反复出现在 minor、minus 与 minute 里：它们都在度量更小或更少的东西。

normal.en: Keep something to a minimum is the everyday frame: whatever follows is the thing you want as small as possible.
normal.cn: keep something to a minimum 是日常框架：后面接的东西，就是你希望尽量压小的对象。

normal.en: Minimum wage and minimum age show the word acting as a modifier without any added ending.
normal.cn: minimum wage 与 minimum age 展示了这个词不靠任何词尾就充当修饰语。

normal.en: Maximum is its opposite, built with the Latin superlative for great, so the pair mark the two ends of a scale.
normal.cn: maximum 是它的反面，用拉丁语表示「大」的最高级构成；这一对词标出一段标度的两端。

abstract.en: Picture a red line near the floor of a measuring tube: everything must stay above it.
abstract.cn: 想象量筒底部附近有一道红线，所有东西都必须停在它上面。

abstract.en: A minimum is not zero; it is the lowest point that still counts as acceptable.
abstract.cn: minimum 并不是零，而是仍然算得上合格的最低点。

abstract.en: Every curve that dips has a floor, and English uses one Latin word for that floor.
abstract.cn: 每条下探的曲线都有一个底，英语用一个拉丁词来指这个底。

examples.en: Keep the noise to a minimum after ten.
examples.cn: 十点以后把噪音降到最低。

examples.en: The river reaches its minimum in late summer.
examples.cn: 这条河在夏末降到最低水位。

examples.en: The minimum age for driving is eighteen in many countries.
examples.cn: 许多国家的驾车最低年龄是十八岁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷你闷」——空间小得人一进去就发闷，小到不能再小；minimum 是最小值、最低限度。

root: 拉丁语 minimus（最小的）是 parvus（小）的最高级形式；中性形式 minimum 被英语原样借作名词「最小量」。一般认为 minimus 与 minus（较少）、minuere（减少）同属一个词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the least amount; the senses run from an allowed lower limit to an observed low, then to attributive and mathematical uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是最小量；各义项从被允许的下限，走到观察到的低点，再延伸到定语用法与数学术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red line near the bottom of a measuring tube, marking the lowest level allowed.
core.cn: 核心意象：量筒底部附近的一道红线，标出允许的最低水位。

branches.en: a red line that the water must not drop below
branches.cn: 水位不得低于的那道红线

branches.en: a river shrinking to its shallowest week
branches.cn: 河水缩到最浅的那一周

branches.en: a sign at the gate stating the youngest age allowed
branches.cn: 门口写明最低年龄的牌子

branches.en: a curve dipping to a single low point
branches.cn: 曲线下探到唯一的最低点

branches.en: a rulebook with its floor printed in bold
branches.cn: 把下限印得又粗又醒目的规章

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin superlative for small, and its family spreads across adjectives, verbs and nouns about making things less.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「小」的最高级构成，它的一族词散落在形容词、动词与名词里，都与「使之更少」有关。

latinIntro.en: Minimum is the neuter form of the Latin superlative for small, and the same root runs through minor, minus and minimize.
latinIntro.cn: minimum 是拉丁语「最小」最高级的中性形式，同一词根贯穿 minor、minus 与 minimize。

definition_en: to ask for something firmly, or the need that people have for a thing
core_image: 一只手伸到柜台前，掌心向上，等着对方把东西递过来
scene: 柜台前排队的人越来越多，店员却只有两个，队伍里开始有人提高声音。 The workers demanded a clear answer about their pay.
sceneCN: 这里 demand 指「要求」（第 1 个义项：坚决地提出要求）；句意是工人们要求就工资给出明确答复。

senses.title: Ask for something firmly
senses.definition: to ask for something in a strong way that expects an answer
senses.definitionCN: 以强硬、期待答复的方式提出要求
senses.example: The workers demanded a clear answer about their pay.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们要求就工资给出明确答复。
senses.why: A request becomes a demand when the asker will not take silence for an answer.
senses.whyCN: 当提问者不肯把沉默当作答复时，请求就变成了要求。

senses.title: The need for a product
senses.definition: the amount of a product or service that people want to buy
senses.definitionCN: 人们想购买的产品或服务的数量
senses.example: There is a growing demand for small electric cars.
senses.exampleCN: 小型电动汽车的需求在增长。
senses.why: Want becomes demand when it is strong enough to reach the market.
senses.whyCN: 当想要的力度大到愿意掏钱，想要就成了需求。

senses.title: Need time or effort
senses.definition: to need a particular quality, time or effort in order to be done
senses.definitionCN: 完成某事需要某种品质、时间或精力
senses.example: Learning a language demands patience.
senses.exampleCN: 学一门语言需要耐心。
senses.why: Some tasks ask for qualities the way people ask for help.
senses.whyCN: 有些任务索要品质，就像人开口求助一样。

intro.en: Demand reached English through Old French, but its parts are Latin: de- meaning fully and mandare meaning to hand over or order.
intro.cn: demand 经古法语进入英语，零件却是拉丁的：de- 表示完全，mandare 表示交付或命令。

items.en: Demandare joined de-, meaning fully, to mandare, to hand over or order.
items.cn: demandare 由 de-（完全）与 mandare（交付、命令）合成。

items.en: Demander could ask a question or make a claim in court.
items.cn: demander 既可以提问，也可以在法庭上提出主张。

items.en: English borrowed it as both a verb of asking and a noun of claim.
items.cn: 英语把它借来，既作表示询问的动词，也作表示主张的名词。

items.en: Economists gave the noun its sense of want backed by money.
items.cn: 经济学家给这个名词添上了「有购买力的想要」这一层。

items.en: Today it covers both a firm request and the pull of the market.
items.cn: 如今它既指坚决的请求，也指市场的拉动。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -mand sound, and the meaning group moves from a polite request to a legal claim.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -mand 这一段音，近义组则从礼貌请求一路走到法律上的主张。

entries.definition: to order someone to do something
needing a lot of time and effort
entries.definitionCN: 需要大量时间与精力的

entries.definition: a person who asks for something
to ask for something in a polite way
to need something or make it necessary
entries.definitionCN: 需要某物或使其成为必要

entries.definition: to say that something belongs to you

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hand held out at a counter and end with a market that keeps pulling.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从柜台前伸出的一只手开始，落到一个不停拉动的市场。

normal.en: A hand held out and not pulled back is already a demand.
normal.cn: 一只手伸出去不收回，就已经是要求了。

normal.en: In a shop, want becomes demand when the money is ready.
normal.cn: 在店里，钱准备好了，想要就变成了需求。

normal.en: A task can demand patience the way a customer demands service.
normal.cn: 任务索要耐心，就像顾客索要服务。

normal.en: Two curves meet on a chart: one asks, one answers.
normal.cn: 两条曲线在图上相遇：一条发问，一条回答。

normal.en: Demand and command share a spine; one asks, one orders.
normal.cn: demand 与 command 共用一副骨架：一个请求，一个命令。

abstract.en: Picture a queue that grows longer while the counter stays the same.
abstract.cn: 想象队伍越来越长，柜台却始终只有那么大。

abstract.en: Picture an empty shelf with a note saying sold out.
abstract.cn: 想象一排空货架，上面贴着售罄的纸条。

abstract.en: Picture a palm turned upward and fingers closing slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象一只掌心向上的手，手指慢慢收拢。

examples.en: The workers demanded a clear answer about their pay.
examples.cn: 工人们要求就工资给出明确答复。

examples.en: There is a growing demand for small electric cars.
examples.cn: 小型电动汽车的需求在增长。

examples.en: Learning a language demands patience and daily practice.
examples.cn: 学一门语言需要耐心和每日练习。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 demand 记成「得忙的」：de 像「得」，mand 像「忙的」，订单一来，全厂都得忙起来，这就是要求与需求。

root: 来自拉丁语 demandare，由 de-（完全）与 mandare（交付、命令）组成，经古法语 demander 进入英语。它先是郑重地提出要求，后来又分出经济上的需求，也用来表示事情对时间与精力的索求。

sensesIntro.en: From a firm request at a counter, to the pull of the market, to the effort a task asks of you.
sensesIntro.cn: 从柜台前一句坚决的请求，到市场的拉动，再到任务向你要的时间与力气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm held out and waiting at a counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只掌心向上的手在柜台前等着。

branches.en: The first sense is a request that expects an answer.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是期待答复的请求。

branches.en: When many people want the same thing, the wish becomes a market force.
branches.cn: 当许多人都想要同一样东西，愿望就成了市场力量。

branches.en: A task can also ask, and what it asks for is time or patience.
branches.cn: 任务也会开口，它要的是时间或耐心。

branches.en: A firm request and a market need both push against the world.
branches.cn: 坚决的请求与市场的需要，都在向世界施压。

branches.en: Both the market and a hard task measure how much people will give.
branches.cn: 市场与艰难的任务都在衡量人愿意付出多少。

intro.en: Demand forms a small family around asking, needing and the side of the market that wants goods.
intro.cn: demand 长出一小族词，围绕请求、需要以及市场中想要货物的一方。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is mandare, to hand over or order, with de- adding fullness.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 mandare（交付、命令），前缀 de- 加上了完全的意思。

items.meaning: to ask firmly, or a need

items.exampleCN: 那是一份要求很高的工作。
提出要求的人在外面等。

items.meaning: relating to buyers in a market
items.exampleCN: 他们研究了需求侧的影响。

items.meaning: a line showing how much people will buy

items.exampleCN: 她是一位抢手的设计师。

items.meaning: in a way that asks for much

definition_en: money that you owe to a person or a bank
core_image: 账本上一行还没有划掉的红字
scene: 他把最后一笔欠款还清，账本终于合上了。 It took him six years to pay off the debt.
sceneCN: 这里 debt 指「债务」（第 1 个义项：欠别人的钱）；句意是他用六年时间还清了债。

senses.title: Money that must be paid back
senses.definition: money borrowed and still owed to a person or a bank
senses.definitionCN: 借来尚未还给个人或银行的钱
senses.example: It took him six years to pay off the debt.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了六年才还清这笔债。
senses.why: Borrowing opens a line that stays open until it is closed.
senses.whyCN: 借钱是在账上开一道口子，还清之前它一直敞着。

senses.title: An obligation of thanks
senses.definition: a feeling of duty towards someone who has helped you
senses.definitionCN: 对帮助过自己的人怀有的亏欠之感
senses.example: She owes a debt to the teacher who believed in her.
senses.exampleCN: 她欠那位相信她的老师一份情。
senses.why: Help given freely still leaves a weight to be carried.
senses.whyCN: 别人白给的帮助，也会在心里留下一份要背的重量。

intro.en: Debt goes back to Latin debitum, a thing owed, from debere, to owe; the silent b is a scholar's gift.
intro.cn: debt 上溯到拉丁语 debitum（所欠之物），源于 debere（欠），不发音的 b 是学者的手笔。

items.en: Debitum meant a thing owed, built on debere, to owe.
items.cn: debitum 指所欠之物，来自 debere（欠）。

items.en: Old French dette dropped the b in both sound and spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 dette 在读和写上都去掉了 b。

items.en: English took dette from French and used it for money and favours.
items.cn: 英语从法语借来 dette，既指钱也指人情。

items.en: Scholars restored the b to show the Latin source; the sound stayed as it was.
items.cn: 学者把 b 加回去以显示拉丁来源，读音却没有变。

items.en: The silent b survives as a small monument to Latin.
items.cn: 这个不发音的 b 留了下来，成了拉丁语的一座小纪念碑。

note.en: The look-alike group hides letters that are not spoken, and the meaning group names what is owed.
note.cn: 形近组里都藏着不发音的字母，近义组则都在说「欠着的东西」。

entries.definition: an amount taken out of an account
entries.definitionCN: 从账户中划出的一笔钱

entries.definition: a feeling of not being sure
a short written form of department
money lent that must be returned
a duty that you must carry out
a debt recorded in accounts

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a line in a ledger and end with a favour that no money can clear.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从账本上的一行字开始，落到用钱还不清的那份情。

normal.en: A debt is a door left open until the last payment shuts it.
normal.cn: 债是一扇门，最后一笔还款才把它关上。

normal.en: Interest is time turned into money.
normal.cn: 利息就是把时间换成了钱。

normal.en: The b in debt is heard by no one and seen by everyone.
normal.cn: debt 里的 b 谁也听不见，却谁都看得见。

normal.en: Borrowing feels light in the hand and heavy at night.
normal.cn: 借钱时手上很轻，夜里却沉。

normal.en: Some debts are paid in visits, not in coins.
normal.cn: 有些债要靠探望来还，而不是靠钱。

abstract.en: Picture a red line in a ledger that no one has crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象账本上一行没人划掉的红字。

abstract.en: Picture an empty purse and a calendar full of dates.
abstract.cn: 想象一只空钱包和一本写满日期的日历。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that helped you once, still held out.
abstract.cn: 想象一只曾帮过你的手，还伸在那里。

examples.en: It took him six years to pay off the debt.
examples.cn: 他花了六年才还清这笔债。

examples.en: The company is deep in debt after two bad years.
examples.cn: 公司经历两个坏年头后债台高筑。

examples.en: She owes a debt to the doctor who saved her son.
examples.cn: 她欠那位救了她儿子的医生一份情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 debt 记成「待」：b 不发音像躲起来，剩下 det 念起来像「待」，欠了钱就得一直待着等还。

root: 源自拉丁语 debitum（所欠之物），动词 debere 意为「欠」。古法语作 dette，把 b 从读音和拼写里都去掉了；英语十三世纪借入，十六世纪学者又按拉丁原形把 b 补回拼写，读音仍旧不发，于是留下这个看得见听不见的字母。

sensesIntro.en: From a sum of money owed, to the weight of a kindness that cannot be counted.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一笔要还的钱，到一份数不清的人情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an uncrossed line of red ink in a ledger.
core.cn: 核心意象：账本上一行没有被划掉的红字。

branches.en: The first sense is the sum borrowed and not yet returned.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是借来还没还的那笔钱。

branches.en: Kindness borrows the same shape, though no ledger records it.
branches.cn: 好意也长成同样的形状，只是没有账本记着。

branches.en: Money and gratitude both leave a person owing something.
branches.cn: 钱和恩情，都让人心里欠着点什么。

branches.en: Both senses explain why the word can be paid and also felt.
branches.cn: 两个义项解释了为什么这个词既能「还」，也能「感到」。

branches.en: The second sense lasts longer, because it has no final payment.
branches.cn: 第二个义项更长久，因为它没有最后一次结清。

intro.en: Debt forms a compact family around owing: the person who owes, the state of owing, and the relief of being free.
intro.cn: debt 这一族都围绕「欠」：欠的人、欠的状态，以及无债的轻松。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is debere, to owe; its participle debitum gives the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 debere（欠），其分词 debitum 演变成英语名词。

items.example: The debt was cleared last month.
The debtor asked for more time.
items.exampleCN: 债务人请求宽限一些时间。

items.example: I am indebted to you for your help.
items.exampleCN: 你的帮助让我十分感激。
他们四十岁时已无债一身轻。
不欠债的农夫睡得踏实。

items.meaning: a situation where debts cannot be paid
items.example: The country faced a debt crisis.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家面临债务危机。

items.meaning: the cancelling or easing of debts
items.example: The bank offered debt relief to farmers.
items.exampleCN: 银行给农民提供了债务减免。

items.meaning: a person paid to recover debts
